title: feat(beacon): builder-specs containers and the fulu blinded block's state root
body:
First step of MEV-Boost builder support: the containers the relay flow exchanges, and a way to compute a fulu blinded block's state root. Nothing calls the new public API yet; the next PR (the builder client and the `produceBlockV3` builder path) does.

## What it adds

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| `DOMAIN_APPLICATION_BUILDER` (`0x00000001`), cross-referenced with gloas's `DOMAIN_BEACON_BUILDER` | `types/src/beacon/constants.rs` |
| `ExecutionPayloadHeader: From<&ExecutionPayload>` and `Deserialize` | `types/src/beacon/containers/deneb.rs` |
| builder-specs containers: `ValidatorRegistrationV1`, `BuilderBid`, `BlindedBeaconBlock{,Body}` and their signed forms (electra/fulu shape) | `types/src/beacon/builder.rs` (new) |
| builder-specs' own example files, CC0, pinned at `fce64468` | `types/tests/fixtures/builder_specs/` |
| `assemble_block` split into `full_body`, `unsigned_block` and `post_state`, with no behavior change | `state_transition/src/beacon/block_production.rs` |
| `assemble_blinded_block` | same file |

## The blinded state root: a stand-in payload and two patches

The state transition takes only full payloads. Other clients either generalize their STF over the payload or keep a separate blinded STF (Grandine). `assemble_blinded_block` does neither:

1. it checks `header.withdrawals_root` against the expected withdrawals;
2. it runs `process_block` on a body whose payload is a stand-in: `parent_hash`, `prev_randao` and `timestamp` copied from the builder's header, the expected withdrawals, everything else empty;
3. it patches the two post-state fields that depend on the payload itself, `latest_execution_payload_header` and `latest_block_header.body_root`.

It is fulu only. Fulu is the last fork with blinded blocks (gloas has none), so the `process_block` the argument rests on cannot change under it. The function's doc walks through fulu's `process_block` step by step.

`blinded_and_full_blocks_reach_the_same_state_root` is the guard. Around the same payload, the blinded block must equal `BlindedBeaconBlock::from(full)`, which means the same state root and the same block root. Its state has a withdrawal due and its body a deposit request. Commenting out either patch makes it fail.

## Trust boundary

| Checked here | Left to the caller (next PR) | Trusted to the relay |
|---|---|---|
| withdrawals root, parent hash, prev_randao, timestamp, blob count | response fork version, signature, value, gas limit, `blob_gas_used` | every other header field, execution validity, execution requests |

The last column matches every client reviewed: only an execution client could check those fields, and the payload is revealed only after the proposer signs.

## Tests

- The containers decode builder-specs' examples from JSON and SSZ, re-encode the SSZ byte for byte, and serialize back to the example JSON.
- A blinded block's root equals the full block's on a fully populated block, so a reordered field fails under both presets.
- There is one refusal test per header check, each asserting the specification's exact condition string.
- `make lint` and `cargo test --workspace --profile release-fast --lib --bins` pass.

## Also

`fulu_state` loses a stale `#[allow(dead_code)]` and its doc no longer contradicts the file: it already had a caller, and this adds a second.

title: feat(rpc): a builder API client (getHeader, registerValidator, submitBlindedBlockV2)
body:
Second step of MEV-Boost builder support: an HTTP client for the builder API, and the builder signing domain. Stacked on #694. Nothing constructs the client yet; the next PR adds `--builder` and wires it into `produceBlockV3`, `register_validator` and `blinded_blocks`.

## What it adds

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| `BuilderClient`: `get_header`, `register_validators`, `submit_blinded_block`; `VersionedBid`; `BuilderError` | `rpc/src/beacon/builder_client/` (new), exported from `ethlambda_rpc` |
| `compute_builder_domain(genesis_fork_version)`, with a mainnet known-answer test | `types/src/beacon/signing.rs` |
| `lean_beacon_builder_request_seconds{call, outcome}` | `rpc/src/metrics.rs`, `docs/metrics.md` |
| `reqwest` (the workspace pin, rustls) and `thiserror` as direct dependencies | `rpc/Cargo.toml` |
| A `#[cfg(test)]` axum mock relay, reused by the next PR's endpoint tests | `builder_client/mock_relay.rs` |

## Encoding, call by call

Each call picks its encoding from how MEV-Boost actually handles it:

| Call | Encoding | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `getHeader` | Asks SSZ-first and decodes by the answer's own `Content-Type`. A 406 fails that call with no retry; later calls ask for JSON | Relays often answer JSON without refusing SSZ. A retry would restart the clock the proposer is waiting on |
| `registerValidator` | Always JSON | MEV-Boost forwards the body unchanged to every relay and answers 200 if any one accepts, so SSZ would be lost silently on relays without it |
| `submitBlindedBlockV2` | SSZ first; after its own 415, the same block again in JSON, and JSON from then on | MEV-Boost converts SSZ per relay. A relay used directly answers 415 at once, so the retry costs nothing |

## Strict choices and bounds

- An SSZ bid without `Eth-Consensus-Version` is an error, since builder-specs requires the header on SSZ answers.
- Only electra and fulu bids are accepted (same container). Any other fork is a separate `UnsupportedFork` error, so the caller can count it.
- `submitBlindedBlockV2` succeeds on 202 only.
- Timeouts:
  - `getHeader` uses the configured header timeout, which is also sent as `X-Timeout-Ms` alongside `Date-Milliseconds`.
  - Registration has 10 s.
  - Submission has 5 s, which is at least MEV-Boost's 4 s.
- Answers are capped at 8 MiB and kept error text at 1 KiB.
- Transport errors drop the URL, so credentials in it cannot reach a log.
- Only `http` and `https` builder URLs are accepted, which catches a missing scheme at startup.

## Tests

The client has 27 tests against the mock relay. The mock relay:
- serves signed bids;
- verifies registration signatures under the builder domain;
- records submissions;
- has knobs for the ways real builders differ: refusing SSZ, ignoring `Accept`, answering slowly, leaving out headers, or giving a chosen status.

`make lint` passes, as do the `ethlambda-rpc` and `ethlambda-types` lib tests.

title: feat(rpc): serve and publish builder blocks (fulu)
body:
Fourth step of MEV-Boost builder support. With this PR, a fulu proposer registered through `register_validator` can receive a builder's blinded block from `produceBlockV3` and publish it back through `blinded_blocks`. Stacked on #696.

**Scope:** the beacon node only. The validator client does not yet register, ask for blinded blocks or publish them; that is the next PR. Gloas (the builder API alongside gossip bids) comes after.

## What it adds

| Piece | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `shouldOverrideBuilder` | Read from `engine_getPayloadV5`, carried on the built payload |
| Registration cache | Each validator keeps the latest registration it forwarded to the builder. An entry lasts 2 epochs after it was last sent, and an older timestamp never replaces a newer one |
| Circuit breaker | Keeps the builder out while the node is syncing or the head is optimistic. Also trips on more than `--builder-fallback-skips` (3) consecutive empty slots, on more than `--builder-fallback-skips-per-epoch` (8) empty slots in the last 32, or on more than `--builder-fallback-epochs-since-finalization` (3) epochs since the state's finalized checkpoint |
| Bid validation | Checks, in order: nonzero value, parent hash, prev_randao, timestamp, block number, withdrawals root, blob count and blob gas, gas limit against the registered target, then the BLS signature (`DOMAIN_APPLICATION_BUILDER`). Every refusal is counted by reason |
| Selection | Uses `builder_boost_factor`. The local payload wins iff `local >= factor * bid / 100`. A tie goes local; `shouldOverrideBuilder` beats everything; `u64::MAX` means builder; the default factor is 100. The winner is chosen before assembly, so only one state transition runs. If the chosen block fails to assemble, the other one is used. This includes a local choice falling back to the bid, which Lighthouse would fail instead, following beacon-APIs' "prefer local unless it is not viable" |
| `produceBlockV3` | A builder win answers the blinded block with `Eth-Execution-Payload-Blinded: true` and the bid's value. A local win answers as before |
| `POST /eth/v2/beacon/blinded_blocks` | Fulu, SSZ or JSON. Checks the parent, the proposer and its signature, claims the slot, then submits to the builder on a spawned task. The builder's 202 becomes 200 and its 400 is passed through; anything else is a 500. There is no local fallback, since that would be a second block |
| Slot guard | `post_block`, the gloas `post_block` and `blinded_blocks` all claim the slot after the signature check and before anything leaves the node. A different root for a claimed slot gets a 400, and so does a slot below the finalized slot |
| Metrics | `lean_beacon_builder_bid_rejections_total{reason}`, `lean_beacon_builder_payload_source_total{source}`, `lean_beacon_builder_fallback_total{reason}` |

## Known limitations

- **The slot guard is in memory and per node.** A restart forgets it, and two beacon nodes behind one validator client do not share it. It stops this node from handing out two different blocks for a slot, which is the case the builder flow adds. It is not slashing protection.
- **Registered proposers wait for the bid.** The header request runs alongside the local build and is bounded by `--builder-header-timeout` (1 s), so it adds at most the difference.
- **Block assembly still runs on the async runtime,** as the local path already did. Moving it onto a blocking task is a follow-up.
- **Not checked, as in every client reviewed:**
  - the bid's fee recipient (relays pay with a transaction; see `docs/spec_deviations.md`);
  - its execution requests;
  - the header fields only an execution client could verify.

## Tests

- Bid validation: one case per check.
- Selection: a table of local and bid outcomes.
- Circuit breaker: every trip, plus edges near genesis and across the `block_roots` wrap.
- Registration cache.
- `produceBlockV3` against the mock relay:
  - builder win;
  - local win;
  - override;
  - boost factor;
  - relay down;
  - invalid bid;
  - both sides failing.
- `blinded_blocks`:
  - accepted;
  - builder 400;
  - builder 500;
  - the claim surviving a failed submit;
  - the cross-endpoint guard;
  - the body limit.
- CLI flags.

`make lint` passes, as do the rpc lib tests and the binary's tests.
author: MegaRedHand

title: feat(validator): propose builder blocks (fulu)
body:
Fifth step of MEV-Boost builder support: the validator client side. With `--builder-proposals`, the client registers its validators with the beacon node's builder and accepts a blinded block when the builder's bid wins. It signs the blinded block and publishes it back to the node that produced it. Stacked on #704.

**Scope:**
- **Covered:** fulu and earlier (electra blinded blocks are accepted for third-party beacon nodes).
- **Gloas is unchanged:** `produceBlockV4` keeps its self-build configuration, and registrations stop at the gloas fork. The gloas builder API comes in phase B.

## Flags

| Flag | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `--builder-proposals` | Off by default. Registers validators and sends `builder_boost_factor` with every pre-gloas block request |
| `--builder-boost-factor <u64>` | Default `100`. Requires `--builder-proposals` |
| `--prefer-builder-proposals` | Sends `u64::MAX`, so the builder wins whenever there is a valid bid, unless the execution client asks to override the builder. Requires `--builder-proposals`; conflicts with `--builder-boost-factor` |

Without `--builder-proposals`, nothing changes: the client sends `builder_boost_factor=0` and refuses a blinded answer, as before.

## What it adds

| Piece | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Registrations | One `ValidatorRegistrationV1` per validator the node resolved, signed under the builder domain (genesis fork version, zero validators root). The signature and timestamp are cached until the validator's fee recipient or gas limit changes. The full set is sent after each epoch refresh and changed keys every slot, in batches of 500, to every configured node, on spawned tasks with signing off the async runtime. Validators with no fee recipient are skipped with one warning |
| Blinded answer | `ProducedBlock` gains a blinded variant. Its root is the full block's, so the proposal guard and the signing path are unchanged. Slot and proposer are checked as for a full block. The fee-recipient check is skipped, since the header names the builder's address |
| Blinded publish | `POST /eth/v2/beacon/blinded_blocks`, SSZ, **only on the node that produced the block**, with no failover: only that node's builder holds the payload, and only that node claimed the slot. The request runs on a spawned task, so the proposal budget cannot cut it off |
| Unconfirmed publish | A 5xx, a timeout, or a publish that outlives the proposal budget is reported as "unconfirmed", not as a missed proposal: the relay may still publish the block. Nothing retries, since the slot is signed and a second block would be an equivocation. A 4xx, a 503 or a refused connection is a definite failure, counted as a failed proposal even when it arrives after the budget, by the publish task itself |
| Metrics | `ethlambda_validator_builder_registrations_sent_total`, `..._builder_registration_failures_total`, `..._blinded_blocks_proposed_total`, `..._blinded_blocks_unconfirmed_total` |

## Known limitations

- **No slashing-protection record,** as for every block this client signs. The in-process guard covers blinded blocks the same way.
- **Per-validator builder toggles** (Lighthouse's `PATCH` route) are out of scope; the flags apply to the whole process.
- **A registration whose send fails is not resent until the next epoch's full send,** even though it is cached right away.

## Tests

- **Unit:** the blinded decode and its root, the HTTP query and status mapping, producer-only publish in the fallback, the registration signature domain, the cache and batching, the gloas stop, the proposal path's outcomes, and the flags.
- **End to end through ethlambda's own beacon node and the mock relay:**
  - registration → blinded produce → sign → publish → relay;
  - a full block when builder proposals are off;
  - a full block when the relay is down.

`make lint` passes, as do the validator lib, rpc lib and binary tests.
author: MegaRedHand

title: feat(validator): publish proposer preferences (gloas)
body:
First gloas step of the builder work: the validator client publishes signed proposer preferences (fee recipient, target gas limit) for its gloas proposals. Stacked on #705.

**Why:** from gloas, beacon-APIs makes `SignedProposerPreferences` the source of a proposer's fee recipient and gas limit, superseding `prepare_beacon_proposer`. A proposer without preferences also gets no trustless bids: p2p bids for its slot are ignored.

## What it adds

| Piece | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Publishing | Every slot, for the current and next epoch that are gloas epochs (so warm-up starts one epoch before the fork). Fetches **v2** proposer duties, whose `dependent_root` is the shuffling dependent root the preferences must carry; the duty loop keeps v1. Signs each own duty whose slot has not started and which was not yet published for that `(slot, dependent_root)`. Submits **one preference per request** to every node, so one refusal does not hold back the others. A reorg that moves the dependent root re-publishes |
| Unconditional | Not gated on `--builder-proposals`, as in Lighthouse: from gloas the preferences carry the fee recipient for every proposal. Validators with no fee recipient are skipped, with one warning per epoch |
| Signing domain | `DOMAIN_PROPOSER_PREFERENCES` at the fork version of `proposal_epoch - 1`, which is what the gossip rule verifies against. The validator guide's head-state signer differs only for a proposal in a fork's first epoch signed during that epoch; ours is the one peers following the gossip rule accept. ethlambda's beacon node accepts both |
| `Eth-Consensus-Version` | The target epoch's fork (gloas) |
| Gloas boost factor | With `--builder-proposals`, `produceBlockV4`'s body carries the configured `builder_boost_factor`, so pooled p2p bids can win on value. Without it the factor stays `0` |
| Metrics | `ethlambda_validator_proposer_preferences_published_total`, `..._failures_total` (preferences a node refused or did not take), `..._duty_fetch_failures_total` (failed v2 duty fetches). A refusal is warned once per preference, then logged at debug |

## Known limitations

- **Lighthouse at the fork boundary (unverified).** It is reported to sign at the proposal epoch's fork version. If its gossip validation also verifies at that version, Lighthouse peers would reject our preferences for the first gloas epoch. Ours follow the spec's gossip rule.
- **A preference cannot be replaced for the same slot and dependent root,** so a fee recipient changed after publishing applies from the next dependent root on.

## Tests

- **Unit:** the v2 path; per-entry submission; refusal isolation; reorg re-publish; the pre-gloas gate; started slots; missing fee recipients; single-flight polling; the fork-version choice on both sides of the boundary; the boost factor in the gloas body.
- **End to end through ethlambda's own beacon node:** preferences signed by the validator client from its own v2 duties pass the node's gossip rules and are gossiped.

`make lint` passes, as do the validator lib, rpc lib and binary tests.
author: MegaRedHand

title: ci: add a Commit-Boost check to the kurtosis battery
body:
Adds a Commit-Boost check to the kurtosis battery: ethlambda builds blocks through Commit-Boost's PBS module, the MEV-Boost replacement that speaks the same builder-API.

## What it runs

`tooling/kurtosis-assertoor/commit_boost_params.yaml`:
- **Participants:** the base battery's three (lighthouse bootnode; lighthouse with the ethlambda validator client; ethlambda beacon node with the ethlambda validator client).
- **MEV:** `mev_type: commit-boost`. ethereum-package then adds a flashbots relay, an rbuilder with its own lighthouse, and one Commit-Boost PBS sidecar per participant.
- **Transactions:** spamoor at a light load (10 transfers and 1 blob transaction a slot). rbuilder submits no bid for an empty block, and spamoor's default load slowed the relay past Commit-Boost's 950 ms getHeader timeout.
- **Images:** the relay, builder, PBS and spamoor images are pinned by digest, since the package's defaults are floating tags.
- **No assertoor:** its checks still fail on the unrelated `GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH` spec mismatch (README, "Known failure").

`scripts/check-builder-blocks.sh` polls Prometheus metrics until all of these hold, or 40 minutes pass:

| Service | Condition | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| ethlambda beacon node | `lean_beacon_builder_registrations_total{outcome="forwarded"} >= 1` | registrations reach Commit-Boost |
| ethlambda beacon node | `lean_beacon_builder_payload_source_total{source="builder"} >= 1` | `produceBlockV3` served a builder block |
| ethlambda VC on ethlambda | `ethlambda_validator_builder_registrations_sent_total >= 1`, `ethlambda_validator_blinded_blocks_proposed_total >= 1` | the validator client registers and publishes blinded blocks |
| ethlambda VC on lighthouse | `ethlambda_validator_blinded_blocks_proposed_total >= 1` | the validator client works against a third-party beacon node |

The script writes each service's builder metrics and the unmet conditions to the results directory on every exit.

## Dispatch only, for now

- **Why:** the image that pushes and pull requests test (`main`'s) has no `--builder` or `--builder-proposals` until the builder stack (#694 to #705) lands. The new `commit-boost` job therefore runs only on `workflow_dispatch` with `battery: commit-boost` or `both`, against an image built from that stack.
- **Unchanged:** push and PR runs keep running only the base battery.
- **Follow-up:** once the stack is on `main`, drop the event condition so the check runs on push too.

## Depends on

- **lambdaclass/ethereum-package#22 (merged, `a15e7df`):** adds ethlambda to `apply_external_builder_flags`.
- **lambdaclass/ethereum-package#23 (open):** gives the MEV builder enode bootnodes. The newest `reth-rbuilder` image refuses the ENRs the package has passed since its 08-05 refactor.
- **The pin:** `COMMIT_BOOST_PACKAGE_REF` is #23's commit, separate from the base battery's `ETHEREUM_PACKAGE_REF`. Re-pin to the merge commit once #23 lands.

## Upstream workarounds

| Breakage | Worked around in |
|---|---|
| rbuilder refuses ENR bootnodes | fork PR #23, through the pin |
| Commit-Boost requires `SECONDS_PER_SLOT`, which the genesis generator no longer writes | an explicit chain in `mev_params.commit_boost_config` (`chain_id` must be a hex string) |

## Tested

- `shellcheck`, `actionlint` and `yq` pass.
- **Local run, passed:** an image built from #707's head (`ae1a3d2f`) met all five conditions about 12 minutes after the enclave started.
  - The relay delivered a builder block in 14 of the 32 slots of epoch 1.
  - ethlambda's beacon node served 1 builder payload out of 16 proposals.
  - Its validator client proposed 1 blinded block; the one behind lighthouse proposed 3.
- **Earlier local runs, failed:** they are why spamoor runs, and at a light load.
  - With no transactions, the relay never held a bid, so every getHeader answered 204.
  - With spamoor's defaults, the validator client behind lighthouse got no bid in 40 minutes.
- **CI:** the job itself has not been dispatched.

title: fix(beacon): cache the anchor's execution hash so its child imports optimistically
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

A checkpoint-synced `ethlambda beacon` paired with an execution client that is still syncing sat at its anchor for up to ~25 minutes, logging `Not importing: the execution client has not validated this block and it is not an optimistic candidate` for the first post-anchor block until it was 128 slots old. Found by ethrex's multisync (lambdaclass/ethrex#7461) on Hoodi: ethlambda parked ~11 minutes and failed the run's 10-minute head-stall check, while Lighthouse in the same setup imports immediately.

It is a spec deviation. `specs/bellatrix/optimistic-sync.md`:

```python
def is_optimistic_candidate_block(opt_store, current_slot, block) -> bool:
    if is_execution_block(opt_store.blocks[block.parent_root]):   # parent.body.execution_payload != empty
        return True
    if block.slot + SAFE_SLOTS_TO_IMPORT_OPTIMISTICALLY <= current_slot:
        return True
    return False
```

and its "Checkpoint Sync" section lets the anchor be assumed `VALID`. ethlambda reads `is_execution_block(parent)` off the execution-hash cache, which was filled only when a block was imported. The anchor is never imported, so its first child looked like the child of a pre-merge block. The same gap made `forkchoiceUpdated` send a zero finalized/safe hash for the anchor, and a restart emptied the cache for every stored block (embedded ethrex restarts a few dozen blocks behind and answers `SYNCING`, so the park could repeat after a restart).

## What Changed

- `SignedBeaconBlock::execution_block_hash_if_execution_block` (types): the one rule for which blocks have an execution hash to cache (the payload hash, minus a pre-merge all-zero one). Import now uses it, with no behavior change.
- `get_forkchoice_store`: caches the anchor's payload hash. Only the hash, no verdict.
- `Store::restore_beacon_scratch`: on resume, rebuilds the cache for the unfinalized `LiveChain` window it already walks, against each block's own slot so pruning still bounds it.
- `docs/beacon_engine.md` and the doc comments: the cache is filled at import, for the anchor, and on resume. The section that described the anchor park as expected behavior now describes the fix.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- Nothing is marked validated: the anchor and resumed blocks get their hash only, so `optimistic_roots`, payload verdicts and `latestValidHash` handling are unchanged.
- Pre-merge bellatrix blocks (zero payload hash), phase0/altair and gloas blocks still cache nothing, so the 128-slot horizon still guards the merge transition and gloas is untouched.
- Behavior change: after checkpoint sync or a restart, the first new block is an optimistic candidate at once; fcU's finalized/safe hash is the anchor's payload hash instead of zero.

## Tests Added / Run

- `execution_block_hash_if_execution_block_gives_post_merge_hashes_only` (types)
- `a_post_merge_anchor_makes_its_first_child_an_optimistic_candidate`, `an_anchor_with_no_execution_payload_caches_no_hash`, plus a gloas-anchor assertion (fork choice)
- `resume_rebuilds_execution_hashes_for_the_unfinalized_window` (storage)
- `cargo test --profile release-fast --lib` for `ethlambda-types`, `ethlambda-storage`, `ethlambda-state-transition`, `ethlambda-blockchain`: all pass.
- Live, on ethrex's multisync (ethrex+ethlambda on Hoodi, Sepolia and Platåberget) with an image of this branch: three full runs passed every EL and CL check on all three pairs, with no `not an optimistic candidate` line in any Hoodi log. Hoodi synced in 24 to 29 minutes. Before the fix, Hoodi failed its first run with the head stuck at the anchor for 10 minutes.

## Related Issues / PRs

- Related to lambdaclass/ethrex#7461 (the multisync check that found it)

title: feat(beacon): add EIP-8450's post-quantum key registry to heze
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

[EIP-8450](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-8450.md) gives every validator and builder a post-quantum key ahead of a signature switch. This PR puts it **in heze**, following the EIP as revised by ethereum/EIPs#12592 and #12599, and its consensus-specs PR, ethereum/consensus-specs#5782. That PR builds the registry as the `eip8450` feature on top of heze; here it is part of heze itself.

This replaces the earlier version of this PR, which added a separate `hstar` fork on top of gloas, following the first draft of the EIP. The EIP has since changed a lot:
- the withdrawal-address path, its execution-layer request and pending queue are gone;
- the BLS signing key is the only authority, with a rate limit and replay protection;
- builders can register;
- a VRF root is stored beside the leanXMSS key.

The PR targets `heze-devnet-3`, the latest heze devnet: EIP-7805, EIP-8015, EIP-8365 and EIP-8198 (quick slots). Testing the registry alongside the other heze components gives a more faithful picture than testing it alone. It also ports the consensus-specs merges since v1.7.0-beta.4 that touch forks up to heze, one commit each.

## What Changed

**The registry (the last commit)**
- **State and body.** Heze's state appends four lists parallel to the validator and builder registries:
  - `post_quantum_key_material`, each index's leanXMSS key plus VRF root, zero for builders;
  - `post_quantum_key_change_epochs`, the epoch of each index's last change;
  - their builder twins.
  Heze's body appends `pq_key_registrations`. Each `active_fields` layout grows by exactly the appended fields, so every earlier field keeps its generalized index.
- **Unset entries.** The gloas upgrade into heze fills the lists. New validators get an unset entry, and so do new builders, a reused builder index included. Shared gloas-family code asks `BeaconState::pq_registry()`, which is `None` before heze, rather than checking the fork.
- **`process_pq_key_registration`** runs last in `process_operations`, in the spec's order. It checks:
  - the registrant: validator or builder, not exiting, an active builder, a zero VRF root for builders;
  - `previous_change_epoch` against the stored change, which blocks replays;
  - the change delay;
  - the registrant's BLS signature;
  - a nonzero key that no index holds;
  - the leanXMSS proof of possession of `PQKeyPossession{pubkey, key}`, at leaf 0.
- **Gossip.** A new `pq_key_registration` topic, on heze digests only. It is validated as the spec's `validate_pq_key_registration_gossip`, IGNORE/REJECT order included. The first-seen record for a pair (index, change epoch) is judged at its spec position, so a later REJECT still wins over a duplicate.
- **Pool, production and API.**
  - The pool keeps one registration per pair, and pruning drops stale or exiting ones.
  - Heze block production packs the pooled registrations that apply after the block's other operations.
  - `GET`/`POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/pq_key_registrations` lists and submits registrations. It is not yet a Beacon API route.
- **Crypto.** `ethlambda_crypto::lean_xmss` verifies through the lean-pq bindings. Nothing in the scheme is reimplemented.

**Spec catch-ups since v1.7.0-beta.4 (six commits)**
- #5736: at the gloas fork, only builder-credential deposits fund builders.
- #5764: voluntary-exit gossip is ignored while the validator has a pending partial withdrawal.
- #5756: slot component durations round to the nearest millisecond, in the node and in the validator client. On this branch the rounding applies to EIP-8198's per-epoch slot duration.
- #5765: fulu's `is_data_available` binds column sidecars to the block.
- #5767: a block without blobs gets no data column sidecars.
- #5763: a doc fix; the code already used the proposal slot.

Already handled here: #5724, #5780, #5768. Not applicable, since there is no implementation of those features: #5737 (partial columns), #5670 and #5788 (fast confirmation). The other merges touch only feature forks heze does not include in the specs (EIP-8025, EIP-8148).

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

**Invariants**
- Each registry list stays exactly as long as the registry it parallels.
- Every applied registration moves its index's stored change epoch forward, so none applies twice.
- A builder index that is reused starts from the new builder's deposit epoch, so a registration signed for the previous builder never applies.

**Behavior changes**
- **`DB_VERSION` 8 → 9:** heze states and blocks change shape.
- **`thiserror` 2.0.18 → 2.0.21**, required by lean-pq, resolved with `make update` under the 14-day cooldown.

**Spec vectors**
- **Heze is now the spec's `eip8450` fork.** The released `heze` vectors lack the registry, so they are listed in `UNMODELED_FORKS`. The `eip8450` directory runs as heze instead.
- **Generating them.** No release ships EIP-8450 vectors yet. `make eip8450-spec-tests` generates them with #5782's pyspec, pinned by commit. It also adds `eip8450` to the forks `ssz_static` covers, in that temporary copy only.
- **Slot duration.** #5782 predates EIP-8198 in heze, so its configs name no `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE`. The harness's existing rule for such fixtures keeps the heze slot duration equal to the genesis one, matching how they were generated.
- **Without them,** the run reports `fixture_forks/missing/eip8450` as ignored, so the gap is visible.
- **Ignored `eip8450` cases.** Its `fork` and `transition` cases start from the registryless heze, so they are ignored.
- **Five beta.4 gloas `fork` cases** are ignored by name, in `SUPERSEDED_BY_5736`. #5736 changed what they expect, and the same cases regenerated at #5736 pass.

**New dependency: `lean-pq`** (ethereum/lean-pq-bindings v0.8.0, pinned by commit). The spec vectors are generated with py-lean-pq, the same bindings, so proofs must verify under exactly that scheme. The `leanvm` pin here is the lean chain's XMSS (BLAKE2s, 42 chains, one tree), a different scheme. The two leanVM revisions coexist as separate crate graphs.

## Tests Added / Run

Runs were kept to what the change needs.
- **EIP-8450 vectors** generated from #5782 at `b1b194cb`, minimal preset, run as heze on `heze-devnet-3`: **10,366 passed, 0 failed**. This covers:
  - all 52 `operations/pq_key_registration` cases;
  - all 21 `networking/gossip_pq_key_registration` cases;
  - `ssz_static` for the new and modified containers;
  - heze's sanity, epoch, fork-choice and gossip suites at the `eip8450` shape.
  The ignored are the `fork`/`transition` cases and topics the node does not validate.
  The #5782 head has since merged master; that brings only spec fixes already ported here, no EIP-8450 change.
- **Gloas fork vectors** regenerated at the same commit: **44/44 pass**, which verifies the #5736 port.
- **Unit tests:**
  - 35 registry tests with real BLS and leanXMSS keys, covering each operation rule, gossip ordering, packing and pruning;
  - the slot-component rounding, EIP-8198 quick-slot timing and validator slot-clock tests, where the #5756 port meets EIP-8198;
  - registry list helpers, `XmssSignature` encoding, and the lean-pq wrapper.
- **Checks:** `cargo fmt --check` passes, and clippy `-D warnings` is clean on the workspace and on the `beacon-spec-tests` target.

Not run, to save compute: the mainnet preset of the vectors, the full beta.4 suite, and the whole-workspace tests. CI covers those.

## Related Issues / PRs
- EIP-8450: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-8450.md, revised by ethereum/EIPs#12592 and #12599
- Spec: ethereum/consensus-specs#5782
- Bindings: ethereum/lean-pq-bindings (v0.8.0)

## ✅ Verification Checklist

- [x] Ran `make fmt`: clean
- [x] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`): clean
- [ ] Ran `make test`: only the impacted tests and the generated EIP-8450 vectors, listed above

title: docs: describe ethlambda as a Beacon Chain and Lean Chain client
body:
## Motivation

The project's self-descriptions still called ethlambda a Lean consensus client only, and `CLAUDE.md` said it was "not to be confused with" a Beacon Chain client. Since `ethlambda beacon` follows the Beacon Chain, those statements are wrong.

## Changes

Every place that describes what ethlambda is now says "Beacon Chain and Lean Chain client":

| File | What changed |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | Tagline; "Current status" now names both chains (beacon side points at the follower quickstart) and scopes the existing bullet list to the Lean Chain |
| `book.toml`, `docs/introduction.md` | Book description and intro. The intro also gains the **Beacon Chain** part that `SUMMARY.md` already lists ("four parts" was five) |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `Dockerfile` (image label), `.github/prompts/ai-review.md` | One-line descriptions |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Replaces "not to be confused with Beacon Chain clients" with the two sub-commands |
| `docs/infographics/*.html` | Subtitle and footer only |
| `docs/lmd_ghost.md` | The comparison table and paragraphs credited "ethlambda" with having no proposer boost or equivocation discounting; that is only true of the Lean Chain, since the beacon fork choice implements both. Scoped to the Lean Chain |

Pages that spoke of "ethlambda" or "the node" while meaning the Lean Chain alone now say so. The Lean content itself is unchanged:

| File | What changed |
|---|---|
| `docs/3sf_mini.md`, `docs/lmd_ghost.md`, `docs/slots_and_intervals.md` | The "In ethlambda" notes become "In ethlambda's Lean Chain" (one said every validator has equal weight, which beacon does not do). The 3SF-mini and LMD-GHOST intros name `ethlambda node`, and LMD-GHOST points at the beacon fork choice |
| `docs/architecture.md` | A scope note: the page describes `ethlambda node`; `ethlambda beacon` runs the same two actors without keys, aggregation or duties |
| `docs/benchmarking.md` | `synthetic` is Lean Chain block building, `import` is Beacon Chain block import |
| `docs/metrics.md` | leanMetrics applies to the Lean Chain; points at where the beacon metrics are |
| `docs/fork_choice_visualization.md` | Served by `ethlambda node` only (`/lean/v0` is a 404 on beacon) |
| `docs/introduction.md` | Spec deviations cover consensus-specs too |
| `README.md` | The `node` section no longer claims the rest of the README is about it |

Left as is, since they already describe the Lean side specifically: `docs/cli.md`, `docs/checkpoint_sync.md`, `docs/beacon_stf.md`, the README's per-sub-command headers, `.claude/skills/*`, and code comments.

## Open questions

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` still says "Lean Consensus is a clean slate. Don't add backward compatibility for deprecated features." The beacon side carries phase0 through gloas by necessity. Should that bullet be scoped to the Lean Chain?
- The architecture infographic's body is all Lean (3SF-mini badge, lean actors); only its subtitle changed here.
- The README roadmap still lists execution client integration as future work.

title: fix(p2p): stop warning on every gossipsub IHAVE dropped by a full send queue
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation
- A beacon node on Hoodi logs `WARN libp2p_gossipsub::behaviour: Send Queue full. Could not send Rpc.` once per heartbeat for every slow peer, each line listing every IHAVE message id of an attestation subnet. The drop is already counted in the peer's `failed_messages` and charged to its score, so the warning adds noise, not information.
- The line is emitted inside the gossipsub crate, so the fix is in the libp2p fork: lambdaclass/rust-libp2p#1 logs non-priority drops (IHAVE, IWANT, publish, forward) at DEBUG and keeps WARN for control drops (GRAFT, PRUNE, IDONTWANT), which do leave the peer's mesh view out of step with ours. This PR picks that commit up.

## What Changed
- `crates/net/p2p/Cargo.toml`: both `rev` fields (`libp2p`, `libp2p-mplex`) move from `2f14d0ec` to `da141177`, the fix commit, whose parent is `2f14d0ec`. The dependency tree therefore differs from today's by those lines only. The branch head was deliberately not taken: it is 51 commits and a full upstream merge ahead (protobuf back to prost, gossipsub behaviour and config changes), which is not a change to make during the 1.0 window.
- `Cargo.lock`: the 38 fork source lines, rewritten in place. `cargo update -p libp2p` was not used because it also re-resolved two unrelated edges (`data-encoding-macro-internal` → `syn`, `iana-time-zone` → `windows-core`); `cargo metadata --locked` accepts the rewritten lock without changes.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees
- No behaviour change beyond the level of one log line. The failed-message counters and the slow-peer scoring are untouched, and control-message drops still warn.
- Nothing else pins the fork revision: the event-monitor lockfile and the Shadow patch do not reference libp2p.

## Tests Added / Run
- `cargo clippy --locked -p ethlambda-p2p --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --locked --profile release-fast -p ethlambda-p2p`: 360 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- Checked that cargo's checkout of `da141177` carries the WARN/DEBUG split.

## Related Issues / PRs
- lambdaclass/rust-libp2p#1 (the fix). This PR does not wait for it: the commit stays reachable on the fork either way, and the pin was already a non-head commit of that branch.
- Follow-up worth a look: ethlambda does not handle gossipsub's `Event::SlowPeer`. Lighthouse penalizes a peer once it has dropped more than 10 priority messages; we only let the score decay do the work.

- [ ] Ran `make fmt` — no Rust source changed in this repo

title: chore(deps): bump quinn-proto, h2, rkyv and crossbeam-epoch past RustSec advisories
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

`cargo audit` against `main` reports 23 advisories. One of them can be triggered remotely by any peer: `quinn-proto` 0.11.14, the QUIC implementation behind libp2p-quic, our primary transport, is open to remote memory exhaustion from unbounded out-of-order stream reassembly ([RUSTSEC-2026-0185](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0185), CVSS 7.5) and to unbounded growth of pending connection-ID retirements ([RUSTSEC-2026-0339](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0339)). Both need no authentication.

This PR takes every fix that already clears the 14-day publish-age cooldown and needs nothing but a lockfile change.

## What Changed

`Cargo.lock` only, via `make update UPDATE_ARGS="-p quinn-proto -p h2 -p rkyv -p crossbeam-epoch"` (so the cooldown is applied):

| Crate | From → to | Advisories fixed | Reachable here? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quinn-proto` | 0.11.14 → 0.11.19 | 0185, 0339 (and 0338, 0340, 0342) | **Yes**: 0185 and 0339 from any QUIC peer. 0342 is not (libp2p-quic disables datagrams), nor are 0340/0338 (ACK_FREQUENCY not enabled, no unordered reads) |
| `h2` | 0.4.14 → 0.4.20 | 0258 (unbounded empty DATA frames) | Client side only (reqwest); our axum servers are HTTP/1 only |
| `rkyv` / `rkyv_derive` | 0.8.16 → 0.8.18 | 0233, 0234, 0235 | No: pulled in by ethrex-common, which we never feed peer-supplied archives |
| `crossbeam-epoch` | 0.9.18 → 0.9.21 | 0204 (`fmt::Pointer` on an invalid pointer) | No |

`quinn-proto` 0.11.19 adds one new transitive dependency, `rand_pcg` 0.10.2.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- No source changes, and no change to any direct dependency's requirement in a `Cargo.toml`.
- Every new version is semver-compatible with the one it replaces and older than the cooldown; `make cooldown-check` passes.

### Deliberately left out

| Crate | Why not here |
|---|---|
| `rustls` (0285, 0346, 0348, 0349), `rustls-webpki` (0382), `webpki-roots` (0381) | The fixed `rustls` (≥ 0.23.45) needs `rustls-webpki` 0.103.16, published 2026-10-20, which is still inside the cooldown: the resolver stops at `rustls` 0.23.43, which fixes none of them. A follow-up after 2026-11-03 picks all three up together. |
| `crypto-bigint` 0.5.5 (0387) | Fixed only in 0.7, which needs an upstream `elliptic-curve`/`k256` major bump. |
| `ruint` 1.18.0 (0220) | Reached through leanVM's `xmss` → `ethereum_ssz`; the fix pulls in `ark-ff` 0.6, so it belongs with a leanVM bump. |
| `hickory-proto` (0118, 0119), `quick-xml` (0194, 0195), `zstd-sys` (0410) | Not reachable: libp2p's DNS/mDNS transports are compiled (`full`) but unused, `quick-xml` only serves `inferno`'s SVG output under `jemalloc_pprof`, and the `zstd-sys` issue is wasm-only. |

After this PR `cargo audit` reports 13 advisories, none of them in `quinn-proto`, `h2`, `rkyv` or `crossbeam-epoch`.

## Tests Added / Run

None added: no source touched.

- `make cooldown-check`: passes
- `make lint`: clean
- `make test`: 2859 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo audit`: 23 → 13 advisories

## Related Issues / PRs

- Follow-up: `rustls` / `rustls-webpki` / `webpki-roots` once `rustls-webpki` 0.103.16 clears the cooldown (2026-11-03).

title: fix: cap gossipsub's log output at ERROR unless RUST_LOG raises it
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation
- A beacon node on Hoodi logs `WARN libp2p_gossipsub::behaviour: Send Queue full. Could not send Rpc.` once per heartbeat for every slow peer, each line listing every IHAVE id dropped on an attestation subnet. The drop is already counted in the peer's `failed_messages` and charged to its score, so the line adds noise, not information.
- The line is emitted inside the gossipsub crate. Rather than patching the libp2p fork, the node's default log filter now caps that crate at ERROR, which is how an operator sees the dependency's noise anyway. Lighthouse goes further and routes all `libp2p_gossipsub` and `discv5` output to separate files.

## What Changed
- `bin/ethlambda/src/main.rs`: `init_node_logging` builds its filter from `node_log_filter(RUST_LOG)`. With no `RUST_LOG` the directives are `info,libp2p_gossipsub=error`; with one they are `libp2p_gossipsub=error,<RUST_LOG>`. A `RUST_LOG` directive on `libp2p_gossipsub` replaces the cap, one on any other target adds to it, and `RUST_LOG` keeps replacing the `info` floor the way `from_env_lossy` always did. The floor is spelled out because `EnvFilter` only applies a default directive when it was given no directive at all.
- Besides the send-queue line, the cap hides gossipsub's other warnings (bad signatures, substream limits, anonymous-mode field checks), all per-peer protocol violations that peer scoring already handles. Its 19 error sites still show.
- The benchmark and keygen filters are untouched; neither runs a network.
- `docs/beacon_wire.md`: one sentence next to the existing `RUST_LOG` example, saying how to see gossipsub's warnings.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees
- Default output changes only for the `libp2p_gossipsub` target: WARN and below are dropped, ERROR stays.
- `RUST_LOG` semantics are preserved, including the pre-existing quirk that a `RUST_LOG` without its own `info` silences other targets. Verified against tracing-subscriber 0.3.23: an equal-specificity directive added later replaces the earlier one, and `Ordering::Equal` implies the same target, so no other directive is clobbered.
- A bare `RUST_LOG=debug` keeps the cap, since the more specific directive wins; the doc comment says to name the crate.

## Tests Added / Run
- Three tests in `main.rs` drive real events through the filter: default behaviour (INFO floor, gossipsub WARN dropped, gossipsub ERROR kept), the lift via `RUST_LOG=…,libp2p_gossipsub=warn,…` alongside another directive, and the floor-replacement quirk.
- `cargo test --locked --profile release-fast -p ethlambda --bin ethlambda -- tests::node_logging tests::rust_log`: 3 passed.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p ethlambda --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

## Related Issues / PRs
- Supersedes #717 and lambdaclass/rust-libp2p#1, which fixed the same symptom in the fork; both are being closed.
- Follow-up worth an issue: ethlambda does not handle gossipsub's `Event::SlowPeer`. Lighthouse reports a peer after more than 10 priority or 10 non-priority drops, so the peer producing these lines gets disconnected instead of staying in the mesh.

title: fix(blockchain): stop the missing-ancestor walk at an imported block
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

An `ethlambda beacon` (v1.0.0-rc.2) paired with geth v1.17.10 on Hoodi stopped importing at slot 4248640 and stayed there for three hours. Found by ethrex's multisync (lambdaclass/ethrex#7461): the pair failed its 10-minute head-stall check while the same image passed with nethermind and ethrex.

The trigger was geth: mid snap sync, it answered `engine_newPayloadV4` past the 8 s engine ladder, so block 4248641 got no verdict and was dropped, as designed (`ImportOutcome::Held`). What should retry such a block is the next arrival: `process_or_pend_block` resolves the arrival's missing ancestor through `pending_block_parents`, and the DB walk then re-queues the first stored block whose parent has a state.

That resolution is what went wrong. `pending_block_parents` stores the missing ancestor as it was when each block pended. Every descendant of 4248641 had pended while 4248639 was the gap, so all of them pointed at 4248639. Once 4248639 imported and 4248641 was dropped after it, every arrival resolved to 4248639. The DB walk re-queued that already-imported block (a no-op through the "already in the store" early return) and returned before `request_missing_block`, so 4248641 was never retried or requested, and ~900 later blocks stayed parked. Only a re-delivery of 4248642, whose parent is 4248641 itself, could have recovered it, and none came.

The same run's Sepolia pair dropped 11 blocks for lack of a verdict and recovered every time, because its pointers happened to land on the dropped block.

## What Changed

- `process_or_pend_block` (`crates/blockchain/src/lib.rs`): the `pending_block_parents` walk stops at an ancestor that already has a post-state. The existing DB walk then steps through the gap block by block, finds the dropped block, re-queues it, and re-points each pending block it passes at its direct parent.
- `ImportOutcome::Held` doc: a no-verdict block is re-driven by the next arrival that leads to it (from the DB, or by asking the network), not by a timer.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- A walk that never meets an imported ancestor behaves exactly as before.
- Cost: one `has_state` read per pointer step. Normally that is one step, since pointers jump straight to the top of a gap; while a gap opened this way is still open, later arrivals step through it a block at a time.
- Not changed: a no-verdict block is still dropped, and only an arrival that leads to it retries it. Nothing retries it on a timer.
- The code path is chain-agnostic, so lean gets the same guard.

## Tests Added / Run

- `a_block_dropped_below_an_imported_ancestor_is_retried_by_the_next_arrival`: an imported ancestor, its child dropped with no state, a grandchild still pointing at the ancestor, then one arrival. Asserts the dropped block is what gets queued. Without the guard it fails, queueing the imported ancestor instead.
- `cargo test -p ethlambda-blockchain --lib --profile release-fast`: 292 passed, 43 ignored.
- Not yet verified live.

## Related Issues / PRs

- Related to lambdaclass/ethrex#7461 (the multisync check that found it)

title: chore(p2p): switch libp2p from the lambdaclass fork to upstream 0.57.1
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation
- Replaces the `lambdaclass/rust-libp2p` fork (rev `2f14d0e`) with the crates.io release `libp2p 0.57.1`, and takes `libp2p-mplex 0.44.0` from crates.io too.
- The fork's only change of its own was `send_request_with_protocol`. Nothing calls it since req/resp became one `request_response::Behaviour` per protocol, so the fork now only costs rebasing.
- **Draft until the dependency tree clears the 14-day publish-age cooldown, on 2026-11-09 04:00 UTC** (see below).

## What Changed
- `crates/net/p2p/Cargo.toml`: `libp2p = "0.57.1"` and `libp2p-mplex = "0.44.0"` instead of the git dependency.
- `Cargo.lock`: re-resolved. Every new crate is pinned to its newest release past the cooldown, except the four listed below. `main` is merged in, and #718's `quinn-proto`, `h2`, `rkyv` and `crossbeam-epoch` bumps are kept.
- `crates/net/p2p/src/lib.rs`: a `Gossipsub` alias that keeps `AllowAllSubscriptionFilter`, and `max_publish_messages(500)` in place of the removed `max_messages_per_rpc(Some(500))`.
- `crates/net/p2p/src/beacon/scoring.rs` (tests): use the alias.
- Comments in `lib.rs`, `swarm_adapter.rs` and `req_resp/behaviour.rs` that pointed at the fork; the libp2p line in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees
| Upstream change | Effect here |
|---|---|
| gossipsub 0.50 defaults to `MaxCountSubscriptionFilter`: 100 topics per peer and per RPC, and a peer over either limit has its whole subscription RPC ignored | Kept the old behavior with the `Gossipsub` alias. A mainnet peer custodying every column subnet is over the limit from those subnets alone, and every peer doubles its topic set around a fork-digest rollover |
| `max_messages_per_rpc` became `max_publish_messages` | **Behavior change:** an RPC over 500 messages now fails to decode and its inbound stream is closed. The fork processed the first 500 and dropped the rest |
| gossipsub 0.50 caps subscriptions plus control data per inbound RPC (`max_control_message_size`, default 16384 bytes) | Not changed; see the open questions |
| gossipsub 0.50 sends all subscriptions in one hello RPC | Not changed; see the open questions |
| libp2p-quic 0.14 prefers the X25519MLKEM768 key exchange | Brings `aws-lc-rs` (a C build) into rustls. The Docker builder already has a C toolchain |
| libp2p-swarm 0.48 smart dialing is opt-in (`with_smart_dial`) | QUIC-first dialing under `DIAL_ADDRESS_CONCURRENCY` is unchanged |
| libp2p-swarm pins `wasm-bindgen-futures = "=0.4.58"` | Moves `wasm-bindgen`, `js-sys` and `web-sys` back in the lockfile |

### Publish-age cooldown
Four crates have no release old enough yet:

| Crate | Published | Clears the cooldown |
|---|---|---|
| `libp2p-peer-store 0.1.0` | 2026-10-15 | 2026-10-29 21:27 UTC |
| `libp2p 0.57.1` | 2026-10-15 | 2026-10-29 21:40 UTC |
| `ctutils 0.4.6` | 2026-10-25 | 2026-11-08 23:01 UTC |
| `crypto-bigint 0.7.10` | 2026-10-26 | 2026-11-09 04:00 UTC |

No older libp2p avoids the last two. Every `libp2p 0.57.x` needs `libp2p-identity ^0.3`, which reaches `crypto-bigint ^0.7.5` through `k256 0.14` (our secp256k1 node keys) and `elliptic-curve 0.14.1`. `crypto-bigint` 0.7.0 to 0.7.8 are all yanked over a breaking fix (RustCrypto/crypto-bigint#1373), so 0.7.9 and 0.7.10 are the only candidates, and both are under two weeks old.

The `Dependency cooldown` job will pass with a warning until then: its probe cannot resolve `libp2p ^0.57.1` under the cooldown, and a failed probe only warns. While it fails, it checks nothing else in the lockfile. I ran the same probe locally with only these four crates held locked: nothing else in the lockfile is too young.

## Tests Added / Run
- `make fmt` and `make lint`: clean.
- `cargo test --profile release-fast -p ethlambda-p2p --lib`: 360 passed.
- `cargo test --profile release-fast -p ethlambda --bins`: 261 passed.
- Not run yet: the full `make test`, and a run against mainnet or devnet peers.

## Open questions
- Should `max_control_message_size` be raised? Upstream rejects an inbound RPC whose subscriptions plus control data exceed it, and does not split its own outgoing IHAVEs to fit.
- A node with `--custody-group-count 128` now announces more than 100 topics in one hello RPC. How do peers that cap subscriptions per RPC treat it?
- Should `features = ["full"]` be narrowed to what we use? That drops `libp2p-peer-store` and the unused transports and protocols.

## Related Issues / PRs
- Related to #718 (merged in; its lockfile bumps are kept).

- [x] Ran `make fmt` — clean

- [ ] Ran `make test` (`test-consensus` plus `test-node`, at `release-fast`) — only `ethlambda-p2p --lib` and `ethlambda --bins` so far

title: feat(cli): store a generated node key in the data directory
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

Without `--node-key`, both sub-commands generated a fresh secp256k1 key in memory on every start, so the node's PeerId and ENR changed on each restart. A lean node lost its place in every peer's scoring. On `beacon` it was worse: the custody columns are a function of the node id, so after a restart the sidecars already on disk belonged to a custody set nobody would select again, and the new id had nothing custodied for it yet. Startup warned about both, and the README told operators to generate a key with `openssl` to avoid it.

This PR makes the node keep its own identity: when `--node-key` is absent, it stores a generated key in `--data-dir` and reads it back on every later start.

## What Changed

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `bin/ethlambda/src/main.rs` | `resolve_node_key(cli, data_dir)`: `--node-key` if given, else `<data-dir>/node.key`, generating and storing it on the directory's first start. Resolution moves below the RocksDB open. New `read_node_key` validates the bytes as a secp256k1 key |
| `bin/ethlambda/src/beacon.rs` | `wire_params` drops its `node_key_supplied` parameter and the custody warning it gated |
| `crates/validator/src/secure_fs.rs` | `secure_fs` module and `write_private` go from `pub(crate)` to `pub`, so the binary writes the key with the same `0600` helper the validator client uses for its secrets |
| `bin/ethlambda/src/cli.rs`, `docs/{cli,architecture,data_storage}.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Describe the new default and the new startup order |
| `README.md` | The quick starts no longer generate a key with `openssl` or pass `--node-key` |

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

```
--node-key given?
├─ yes → read it; nothing is written, a stored node.key is ignored
└─ no  → <data-dir>/node.key exists?
         ├─ yes → read it; a file that fails to load is a startup error, never replaced
         └─ no  → generate, write node.key.tmp (0600), rename to node.key, use it
```

- **The stored key is never regenerated.** A stored file that fails to load (bad hex, wrong length, not a valid secret key) is a startup error naming the path, since replacing it would silently discard an identity that was working.
- **A supplied `--node-key` wins.** Passing it on a directory that already holds `node.key` uses the supplied key and leaves the stored one untouched.
- **Both paths now validate the key at load.** An invalid `--node-key` used to reach `build_swarm` and panic with `invalid node key`; now it is a startup error naming the file.
- **Same format as `--node-key`.** The stored file is hex with a trailing newline, so it can be passed as `--node-key` to another run.
- **Written under RocksDB's lock.** Resolution runs after `RocksDBBackend::open`, so two processes started on one directory cannot both generate a key and race to store it. The `.tmp` + rename means an interrupted first start leaves no partial key.
- **The key sits in RocksDB's own directory.** RocksDB ignores files it did not write; `rocksdb_reopens_a_data_dir_holding_a_stored_node_key` pins that. Wiping the directory resets the identity together with the custody columns it selected.
- The custody warning in `beacon::wire_params` is removed because the identity is now always stable across restarts.
- The Hive test-driver early return still comes before key resolution, so a driver run never touches the data directory.

## Tests Added / Run

Added in `bin/ethlambda/src/main.rs`:
- `a_supplied_node_key_is_read_verbatim_and_nothing_is_stored`
- `a_missing_node_key_is_generated_once_and_reloaded_from_the_data_dir` (also checks that the stored file reads back as `--node-key`)
- `a_generated_node_key_is_stored_at_mode_0600` (unix)
- `a_stored_node_key_that_fails_to_load_is_an_error_not_a_new_key`
- `rocksdb_reopens_a_data_dir_holding_a_stored_node_key`

Run:
- `cargo test -p ethlambda --profile release-fast --bins`
- `cargo test -p ethlambda-validator --profile release-fast --lib`

## Related Issues / PRs

None.

- [ ] Ran `make test` (`test-consensus` plus `test-node`, at `release-fast`) — not run in full; only the two touched crates' unit tests above

title: fix: v1.0.0 release feedback (docker stop, version note, shutdown log, identity metadata, anchor canonical)
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

Fixes from testing the v1.0.0 release (`ethlambda beacon` on mainnet, Docker and the release binary). Four commits, one per finding:

| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| `docker stop` force-kills after 10 s, but a clean shutdown during catch-up took 14.3 s, so the state was lost | README: `--stop-timeout 60` on both `docker run` lines |
| The release binary's `--version` says `-rc.2-` while the image says `-stable-`, and only RELEASE.md explains why | README: one note next to the binary instructions, linking RELEASE.md#version-string (the release notes link this README) |
| Every clean Ctrl+C logged `ERROR ... P2P networking is no longer functional` | The swarm loop's exit is logged at info when the P2P actor shut down; error only when the swarm itself ends |
| `/eth/v1/node/identity` `metadata` was a placeholder (seq 0, no subnets), disagreeing with the ENR's `attnets` | The endpoint reports the live `MetaData` peers get over req/resp |
| `/eth/v1/beacon/headers/head` returned `canonical: false` while the head was still the checkpoint anchor | The beacon bootstrap indexes the anchor's slot in `BlockRoots`, as lean's `init_store` already does |

Not fixed here: `is_syncing` and `/eth/v1/node/health` misreport during catch-up (health `200` while 80+ slots behind). The cause is that the beacon sync tracker's "freshest block seen" counts only imported blocks, so pending gossip blocks during catch-up look like a network stall. Changing that input has a security trade-off (leanSpec counts only signature-valid blocks so a peer cannot fake freshness), so this PR only widens the README caveat.

## What Changed

- **README.md**: `--stop-timeout 60`, the version-string note, and a wider `is_syncing`/health caveat.
- **`crates/net/p2p/src/swarm_adapter.rs`**: `swarm_loop` breaks with a `LoopExit` reason. A channel closed by the P2P actor is a graceful shutdown (`info`). An actor panic looks the same from here, but spawned-concurrency logs it as an error before stopping the actor.
- **Identity `MetaData`**:
  - `ethlambda-network-api` gains `MetaDataController`/`AdvertisedMetaData`, a shared handle in the `SyncStatusController` mould.
  - `BeaconWire` publishes to it at startup and on every sequence-number bump, all of which now go through `BeaconWire::bump_metadata_seq_number` (fork digest switch, sync committee subnet join and leave).
  - `P2P::local_metadata()` hands it to `main.rs`, which puts it in `BeaconIdentity`; `get_identity` reads it per request.
- **Anchor index**:
  - `Store::index_beacon_anchor` writes the anchor's `BlockRoots` row, keyed by the anchor **block's** slot (a checkpoint state sits after its latest block when the epoch's first slot was empty).
  - `get_forkchoice_store` calls it right after inserting the anchor block, and so does the RPC test fixture that mirrors it.
  - Docs in `block_id.rs`, `docs/data_storage.md` and `docs/rpc.md` updated.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- `metadata.seq_number` is the MetaData counter, not the ENR's `seq`: the p2p specification counts the two separately, so they can still differ. `attnets` now matches the ENR.
- With the anchor indexed, `BeaconBlocksByRange` serves the anchor block too (BlocksByRoot already did). Its data columns were never fetched, so a columns-by-range answer still has none for that slot.
- Directories bootstrapped before this change have no anchor row. Slot lookups there keep falling back to `anchored_root_at_slot` (the head, justified and finalized roots). No `DB_VERSION` bump.
- Lean is unaffected: the anchor index is beacon-only and lean has no `MetaData`.

## Tests Added / Run

- `canonical_is_checked_against_the_index` now expects the anchor to be `true` (it pinned the old gap) and adds a non-canonical sibling that must be `false`.
- New: `index_beacon_anchor_keys_the_row_by_the_blocks_slot` (storage), `the_beacon_api_copy_follows_every_change` (p2p), `identity_reports_the_metadata_peers_are_told` (rpc).
- `cargo test --profile release-fast --lib` for `ethlambda-storage`, `-rpc`, `-p2p`, `-network-api`, `-state-transition`, `-blockchain`: all pass. leanSpec fixture tests not run.

- [x] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`) — clean
- [ ] Ran `make test` (`test-consensus` plus `test-node`, at `release-fast`) — only the `--lib` targets above

title: fix(p2p): wait out the peers' backoff before regrafting a left topic
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

On a 7-node all-ethlambda kurtosis devnet (`ethlambda-all.yaml` from our ethereum-package fork, image 1.0.0), every CL logged this at the start of epoch 5, against the same two peers:

```
WARN libp2p_gossipsub::behaviour: [Penalty] Peer attempted graft within backoff time, penalizing peer=...
```

The two penalized nodes had each left an attestation subnet when an aggregator duty expired at the end of epoch 4. At the epoch 5 boundary, the VC's duties for epoch 6 asked for that subnet again, and the node rejoined about 23 s (and, on the other node, 55 s) after leaving. The trigger is a duty on a subnet in the last slots of epoch N, none in N+1, and one in N+2.

The cause is an asymmetry in rust-libp2p gossipsub (verified at our pinned rev `2f14d0e`):

| Side | What it does | Backoff |
|---|---|---|
| Leaver | Sends UNSUBSCRIBE, then PRUNE carrying `unsubscribe_backoff`; won't graft for that long | 10 s default |
| Receiver | Handling the UNSUBSCRIBE, removes the peer from the mesh with `remove_peer_from_mesh(.., None, ..)`; `None` means `prune_backoff`. Backoffs are only ever extended, so the PRUNE's shorter value can't shorten it | 60 s default |

So the leaver regrafts after 10 s into peers still holding a 60 s backoff. They reject the graft and add a behaviour penalty (P7).

## What Changed

- `crates/net/p2p/src/lib.rs`: a `PRUNE_BACKOFF` constant (60 s, gossipsub's default) set as both `prune_backoff` and `unsubscribe_backoff` in `gossipsub_config`, so this node waits as long after leaving a topic as its peers do. Plus a unit test checking that the unsubscribe backoff is at least a default peer's prune backoff.
- `docs/beacon_wire.md`: a third "difference from lighthouse" bullet in Peer scoring explaining the choice.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- The mesh on a rejoined subnet comes back no later than before. The early grafts were rejected anyway, so the subnet's mesh was empty for the peers' 60 s either way; this only stops the node from being penalized for trying.
- No effect on lean: its subscriptions are fixed at startup and never left.
- Severity was low. One penalty per peer per event, and the behaviour penalty only counts past its threshold, so it would take about 10 such events per epoch, sustained, to reach the gossip threshold. Lighthouse would penalize us the same way, since it uses the same rust-libp2p defaults.

**What the specs say**

- consensus-specs (`v1.7.0-beta.2`, `phase0/p2p-interface.md`) fixes `D`, `D_low`, `D_high`, `D_lazy`, the heartbeat, `fanout_ttl`, `mcache_*` and `seen_ttl`, and leaves gossipsub v1.1's extra parameters (backoffs, scoring) "under investigation". For subnets, it asks for `SUBNETS_PER_NODE` long-lived subscriptions held for `EPOCHS_PER_SUBNET_SUBSCRIPTION` epochs. An aggregator joins its duty's subnet (`phase0/validator.md`), but nothing says how long to stay.
- The libp2p gossipsub v1.1 spec recommends a 1-minute `PruneBackoff` and a 10 s `UnsubscribeBackoff`, and expects the leaver's PRUNE to carry the shorter one. rust-libp2p's receiver doesn't honor it, which is the asymmetry above.
- Lighthouse sets neither backoff, and unsubscribes 2 slots after an aggregator duty (`UNSUBSCRIBE_AFTER_AGGREGATOR_DUTY`).

An alternative is to keep an expired aggregator subnet until the next epoch's duty refresh, so the leave never happens in the first place. I didn't take it because it changes subscription logic rather than one parameter, and still leaves other leave-and-rejoin paths exposed.

## Tests Added / Run

- `rejoining_a_topic_waits_out_the_backoff_peers_apply_to_a_leaver` (new)
- `cargo test -p ethlambda-p2p --lib --profile release-fast`: 361 passed, 1 ignored (an existing devnet3 fixture)

body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

With the `include-ethrex` feature, `ethlambda beacon` without `--execution-endpoint` starts [ethrex](https://github.com/lambdaclass/ethrex) in-process and validates payloads through an in-process Engine API transport: every `newPayload`, `forkchoiceUpdated` and `getPayload` is a direct call into ethrex's own handler, with no socket, no JWT and no JSON request body. An explicit endpoint still selects an external client over HTTP, so one image serves both setups.

**Ported from `nightly` to `main`.** The branch was first built on `nightly`, and that build (4424b51c) is what ran on mainnet (see Tests). Moving it onto `main` changed two things beyond the commits themselves:

- `Cargo.lock`: every version `main` locks is kept, and the 367 crates the ethrex dependencies add are at the versions the `nightly` build ran, except `clipboard-win` (Windows-only), moved from 5.4.1 (since yanked; 5.4.2 and 5.4.3 are younger than the cooldown) to 5.1.0 so `make cooldown-check` passes.
- The `ethrex` CI job pins its actions like the rest of `ci.yml` (#713), so `gh actions-lock --verify` passes.

## What Changed

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `Cargo.toml`, `crates/net/p2p` | ethrex bumped v25 to v29.0.1 as a single workspace dependency. Discovery adapts to v29's `DiscoveryServer` (a shared local identity, an execution fork id channel started at `None`); `DiscoveryConfig` gains `nat_extip_set`, tied to `--discovery.advertise-ip` so IP voting cannot override an address the operator chose |
| `crates/net/engine` | `EngineClient` keeps one public API over a private `Transport` enum (`Http` / `InProcess`), so the chain actor and Beacon API handlers do not change. `in_process.rs` builds each ethrex handler struct and calls `RpcHandler::handle` |
| `crates/execution/ethrex` (new `ethlambda-ethrex`) | `start` is ethrex's `init_l1` without its RPC servers; `--ethrex.*` flag subset with `ETHREX_*` env for the rest; opt-in execution JSON-RPC server over the shared context; shutdown after the chain actor joins |
| `bin/ethlambda/src/{cli,main}.rs` | feature-gated wiring: choose embedded vs external client, port clash checks against the beacon node's own ports |
| `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | `make test-ethrex` + CI job `ethrex` (kept out of `test-node` for the runner's disk ceiling); extra clippy pass over the binary's feature-gated code |
| `docs/ethrex.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | flags, lifecycle, how a call works, what is left out |

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

| Build | `--execution-endpoint` given | Execution client |
|---|---|---|
| default | no | none: blocks import without payload validation |
| default | yes | the external client at that endpoint |
| `include-ethrex` | no | **embedded ethrex** |
| `include-ethrex` | yes | the external client at that endpoint; ethrex does not start |

- **The ethrex bump is workspace-wide**, so the default build's discv5 moves to v29 too. The feature does not touch `ethlambda node` (lean), but the dependency does.
- ethrex keeps most `ExecutionPayload` fields crate-private, so a payload goes through `from_block` with the consensus layer's claimed block hash put back: ethrex checks that claim rather than a recomputation. A payload no ethrex block can carry (undecodable transaction, base fee past `u64`) goes to the handler's own JSON `parse`, so ethrex gives the verdict it gives over the wire.
- Errors keep their wire codes (`-38005`, `-38006`, ...). No retry ladder in-process (every error is an answer), but the per-method timeouts stay, since the chain actor awaits `newPayload` inline.
- `start` repeats `init_l1`'s steps, so **when the ethrex pin moves, `init_l1`, `init_rpc_api` and the binary's `server_shutdown` must be re-diffed** against `crates/execution/ethrex/src/lib.rs` (also in the crate docs).
- Known: embedded ethrex restarts up to ~34 blocks below its pre-SIGINT head (state for the newest blocks is not persisted on shutdown) and re-executes them within ~30 s. Not a resync.

## Tests Added / Run

- `crates/execution/ethrex/tests/engine_round_trip.rs`: Engine API round trips against an embedded ethrex, on Osaka and Amsterdam genesis fixtures. Run with `make test-ethrex`.
- Live (on the `nightly` build): mainnet follower on eth-5, binary built from 4424b51c, one process for beacon + ethrex, from 2026-10-24 17:20Z to 2026-10-26 21:14Z. A fresh checkpoint sync on 2026-10-26 (anchor 15516640, ethrex DB kept, ~5500 blocks behind) went optimistic until ethrex caught up, then `sync_distance 0` and `is_optimistic: false` ~14 min after the restart, head matching publicnode.

## Related Issues / PRs

- Related to #605 (`feat/ethrex-discovery-contact-table`, also changes `crates/net/p2p/src/discovery/mod.rs`; will need the v29 `DiscoveryServer` signature)

## ✅ Verification Checklist

- [ ] Ran `make fmt` — clean
- [ ] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`) — clean
- [ ] Ran `make test` (`test-consensus` plus `test-node`, at `release-fast`) — all passing
