title: feat(discovery): hunt attestation subnet peers with discv5 predicate queries
body:
**Draft**: pins ethrex to `8f847524`, the head of ethrex's `feat/discv5-predicate-queries`. That branch has no ethrex PR yet and is built on the open [lambdaclass/ethrex#7217](https://github.com/lambdaclass/ethrex/pull/7217). Not mergeable until both are in an ethrex release and the pin goes back to a tag.

**Includes #605.** This branch merges `feat/ethrex-discovery-contact-table` (#605), since predicate queries are built on the contact-table API that PR migrates to. #605 can be closed in favor of this one, or merged first; the diff here then shrinks to the last three commits.

## Motivation

The dial loop ranks what discv5's crawl happens to find, which only reorders random draws. About one mainnet record in 32 advertises a given attestation subnet, so a subnet this node subscribes to can stay without peers for as long as the crawl takes to stumble on one. ethrex's new `DiscoveryHandle::find_nodes` and `records_matching` let the search be aimed instead, the way Lighthouse uses sigp/discv5's `find_node_predicate`.

## What this does

### 1. ethrex pin bump

`v25.0.0`-based #7217 head (`4462253e`) to `8f847524` (`v30.0.1` + the branch). Builds with no API changes: the contact-table API is the same. The lockfile moves only ethrex crates; `make cooldown-check` passes.

### 2. Subnet hunt (`discovery/subnets.rs`)

```text
 dial tick ── wanted subnets ──► watch ──► hunt task (one hunt at a time)
     ▲                                       │ 1. records_matching: what discovery holds
     │                                       │ 2. find_nodes: walk the DHT for the rest
     └──── admitted peers ◄──── mpsc ◄───────┘
```

| Piece | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| What is short | A **subscribed** subnet (what our `attnets` advertises) with fewer than `TARGET_SUBNET_PEERS` = 3 connected peers advertising it (Lighthouse's number) |
| Predicate | Admission (`LeanFilter`) plus at least one wanted `attnets` bit; the bit test runs first so most records are turned away before anything is decoded |
| Cadence | One hunt at a time on its own task: cached matches first, then a walk of up to 10 s, at most 6 peers per hunt, 30 s between hunts |
| Gating | Nothing is wanted while the dial loop has no budget, so no walk runs for peers nobody would dial |
| Re-offers | A peer a hunt handed over is left out of hunts for 10 minutes: a mainnet peer at its inbound cap connects and says goodbye, and discovery keeps offering it |
| Where finds go | The existing candidate queue. `rank_candidates` gains a tier: custody gaps, then wanted subnets, then any uncovered subnet |
| Metric | `lean_discovery_subnet_hunt_peers_total` |

### 3. ENR sync between discv5 and the API

| Direction | Status |
| --- | --- |
| discv5 → API | **Done.** ethrex writes every record it re-signs (discv5 IP voting) into the `SharedLocalNode` it is spawned with. `discovery::LocalEnr` reads that mirror, and `/eth/v1/node/identity` reads it per request through `ethlambda_rpc::EnrSource` (a closure, since the RPC crate does not depend on `ethlambda-p2p`). |
| ethlambda → discv5 | **Not supported by ethrex yet.** `DiscoveryServerProtocol` has no message that edits the local record. Its only consumer-driven edit, the `fork_id` watch, writes the EIP-2124 `eth` entry, not `eth2`. Writing into the mirror does nothing: discovery serves its own copy and overwrites the mirror on its next edit. So the served `eth2` still keeps the startup digest across a fork boundary (`update_served_enr` still only warns; its doc now says this). What ethrex would need: a protocol message that applies an edit through `NodeRecord::edit` (one `seq` bump, re-signed) and mirrors the result, as `refresh_fork_id` already does for `eth`. |

### Merge resolution with #605

Main had made `LeanFilter` `Clone` with a shared fork-boundary `Policy`; #605 had made it non-`Clone` because discovery takes it by value. Both hold now: clones share the `Policy` and the `DialTargets` map, and `SpawnedDiscovery` carries a clone, so `set_fork_id` still reaches discovery's copy. #605's behavior change is inherited: `--discovery.advertise-ip` sets `nat_extip_set`, so IP voting no longer overwrites an address the operator named.

## Assumptions

- "Subnets we're missing" means **subscribed subnets below 3 connected peers**, not only subnets with zero.
- Duty subnets from a validator client (`beacon_committee_subscriptions`) are **not** fed to the hunt; that stays a separate gap.
- Counts come from the `attnets` of peers dialed from discovery. Inbound peers never show us an ENR, so they count for nothing: the hunt errs toward hunting.

## Testing

- `make lint`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked`, `make cooldown-check`
- `cargo test --workspace --profile release-fast --lib --bins`: all pass. leanSpec spec suites not run.
- New unit tests: the hunt predicate (wanted bit, other network, already offered), `offer`'s limit and dedup, `short_subnets`, the no-budget gate, and the new ranking tier.
- Not covered: an end-to-end hunt across live discovery servers. ethrex's own `discv5_server_tests` cover `find_nodes`; this side tests what it feeds it and what it does with the answer.

## Follow-ups

- Return the pin to an ethrex release tag once #7217 and the predicate-query branch land.
- Feed VC duty subnets to the hunt (with expiry), as Lighthouse and Grandine do.
- Ask ethrex for a local-record edit message, then refresh `eth2` at fork boundaries.
- `records_matching` does not exclude ethrex's tried set, so a hunt can re-offer a peer the contact poll already handed out within the same 10 minutes; the dial loop absorbs it (`AlreadyInProgress`, skip if connected).
author: MegaRedHand

title: feat(validator): durable EIP-3076 slashing protection
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

`ethlambda validator` kept no slashing-protection record. Its two in-memory guards (`AttestationGuard`, `ProposalGuard`) applied EIP-3076's minimal rule within one run, but a restart emptied them and nothing stopped a second process from signing with the same keys. The client warned about this on every start, and `docs/spec_deviations.md` listed it as a known gap. That gap is the blocker for anyone running ethlambda with real stake.

This PR makes slashing protection durable. It is the first of two PRs; the second adds EIP-3076 interchange import/export (CLI and keymanager API).

**Design.** Before choosing, we surveyed Lighthouse, Prysm, Teku, Nimbus, Lodestar and Grandine.

- **Teku's model:** one record per validator holding EIP-3076 *minimal* watermarks (highest block slot, highest attestation source and target). It persists the rule our guards already enforced.
- **Why not full history:** the full-history clients end up enforcing almost the same thing. Lighthouse prunes to one epoch and minifies every import. What full history buys is allowing a byte-identical re-sign after a crash, and it costs a new C dependency (SQLite), pruning and migrations.

## What Changed

- **New `crates/validator/src/slashing_protection/`**:
  - **`mod.rs`, `SlashingProtection`:**
    - the rule: an attestation needs `target > last target` and `source >= last source`; a block needs `slot > last slot`;
    - "never signed" is `None`, so slot 0 and epoch 0 are signable exactly once;
    - `open` and the batch APIs;
    - every change is written to disk first and taken into memory only once the write succeeds.
  - **`file.rs`, the on-disk record:**
    - `<validators-dir>/slashing_protection.json` is an EIP-3076 v5 minimal interchange naming the chain's `genesis_validators_root`;
    - strict reading that fails closed;
    - durable writes: temp file, `fsync`, `rename`, directory `fsync`;
    - an exclusive `File::try_lock` on `slashing_protection.lock`.
- **Signing path:**
  - **`attestation.rs`:** one slot's batch is checked and recorded in a single write, inside `spawn_blocking` and before the store's read lock is taken. Only then are the allowed attestations signed.
  - **`proposal.rs`:** the cheap pre-check stays before `produce_block`. The recording check moves before signing and persists.
  - **Write failure:** a failed write signs nothing.
- **Startup (`lib.rs`):**
  - the record is opened right after `genesis()`, which supplies the root it must match;
  - a key with no record is refused unless `--init-slashing-protection` is passed;
  - the unconditional "keeps NO slashing-protection record" warning is replaced by an info line.
- **Keymanager:** `POST /eth/v1/keystores` registers each imported key before writing it to disk or loading it.
- **Removed:** `attestation_guard.rs` and `proposal_guard.rs`. Their rule and tests moved into `slashing_protection`.
- **New metrics:** `ethlambda_validator_slashing_protection_write_seconds` and `ethlambda_validator_slashing_protection_write_failures_total`.
- **Docs:**
  - `docs/spec_deviations.md`: the section is rewritten to describe the minimal-watermark deviation.
  - `docs/cli.md` and `README.md`: the new flag and the slashing-protection callout.
  - `docs/metrics.md` and `CLAUDE.md`: updated to match.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- **Ordering:** check, then a durable record, then the signature. A signature that exists is always one the record already accounts for, whether the process then crashes, hits its duty deadline, or is rejected by the beacon node.
- **Fail closed:** startup stops on any of these, never reading them as "nothing signed":
  - an empty, malformed or wrong-version file;
  - a validator listed twice;
  - a record for another `genesis_validators_root`;
  - a key with no record.

  At signing time, an unregistered key or a failed write refuses the message.
- **One process:** a second validator client on the same `--validators-dir` refuses to start while the first holds the lock.
- **Behavior change for operators:** the first start after upgrading refuses with a message naming `--init-slashing-protection`. That flag registers each key as if it had signed a block and an attestation at the current slot and epoch, so it costs at most the rest of the epoch. It is still meant only for keys that have signed nothing anywhere for at least two epochs, and it never lowers an existing record.
- **Behavior change for deployments:** `--validators-dir` must now be writable, for the record and its lock. A read-only mount of the keys (a Kubernetes Secret, a `:ro` volume) fails at startup.
- **Known cost:** a byte-identical re-sign after a crash is refused, as in Teku. Documented in `spec_deviations.md`.
- **Not in this PR:** carrying history in or out. Keymanager `DELETE` still returns the empty, all-zero-root interchange, and `POST` still ignores `slashing_protection`. Both are PR 2.

## Tests Added / Run

- **`slashing_protection` unit tests:**
  - every rule case ported from the guards;
  - reopening restores the record;
  - each corrupt-file shape fails `open`;
  - a validator listed twice fails `open`;
  - another chain is refused;
  - the lock refuses a second open and is released on drop;
  - an unknown key is refused without `init` and registered with it;
  - `init` never lowers a record;
  - a failed write (read-only dir) changes nothing;
  - the file is a valid EIP-3076 v5 minimal interchange;
  - a key twice in one batch is refused the second time.
- **Service tests (`MockBeaconNode`):**
  - `a_restart_does_not_forget_what_was_attested`;
  - `a_restart_does_not_forget_what_was_proposed` (no block is even requested);
  - `a_record_that_cannot_be_written_signs_nothing`.
- **Keymanager:** `an_imported_key_is_registered_for_slashing_protection`, where the next start opens without `--init-slashing-protection`.
- **Commands run:**
  - `make fmt`: clean
  - `make lint`: clean
  - `make test`: 2878 passed, 0 failed (after the review follow-ups); the validator crate alone is at 344 after the bot follow-ups

## Review follow-ups (2808b51d)

| Review point | Change |
|---|---|
| Kurtosis battery would fail on `main` | `vc_extra_params: ["--init-slashing-protection"]` on both ethlambda validator clients. The **Assertoor** check on this PR fails for the same chicken-and-egg reason: PR runs test the published `unstable` image, which does not know the flag yet. The post-merge run on `main` tests the merge commit's image, which does |
| Keys registered without history start as "never signed" | `--init-slashing-protection` and keymanager imports now seed the current slot and epoch (block slot = now, attestation target = current epoch). The source stays at 0: seeding it higher would refuse every attestation until justification caught up |
| `path.exists()` fails open | Only `NotFound` counts as absent. A symlink, directory or unreadable path is refused instead of replaced |
| A failed import leaves a record behind | Keys are registered in one write, after they are persisted and before any is loaded |
| Mutex taken on the executor | Every async access (attestations, the proposal pre-check and record, the keymanager) goes through one `slashing_protection::blocking` helper |
| Read-only `--validators-dir` | Documented in `docs/cli.md` |
| Refusal counter undercounts | A failed write counts every refused attestation |
| Permission tests fail as root | Skipped when `geteuid() == 0` |
| Lock described as per key | The docs now say it is per directory |
| Stale "guard" wording | Replaced, including `ProposalRefused` and `is_retryable` |
| Startup error pointed at an import that does not exist yet | Reworded to the wait condition (import arrives in #736) |
| Cleanups | The durable write moved to `secure_fs::write_private_durably` and is shared with `validator_definitions.yml`, which gains its missing fsyncs. No clone of the record per write, compact JSON, one write per keymanager import |

## Bot review follow-ups (696e2a80)

| Review point | Change |
|---|---|
| macOS: directory `fsync` is not `F_FULLFSYNC` (Kimi 4) | The directory flush after the rename calls `File::sync_all` first, `F_FULLFSYNC` on macOS like the file's own flush, and falls back to a plain `fsync` only where a filesystem refuses that for a directory. The original error is kept if both fail |
| File mode and the deterministic `.tmp` path (Kimi 5, 11) | The umask itself was not a problem (it can only clear bits from `0600`), but a leftover `.tmp` from a crashed write kept its old mode, since `mode()` applies only at creation. The temporary is now removed first and created with `create_new`, so the record never inherits a wider mode and a symlink planted at the `.tmp` path is never written through. Two tests pin both |
| Poison vs. disk failure, string errors (Kimi 1, 9) | `slashing_protection::blocking` returns the crate's `Error` instead of a `String`. A poisoned lock, or a panic inside the operation, is the new `SlashingProtectionUnusable`, whose message says the client must be restarted; a failed write stays `Io`. Never retryable |
| Duplicate-key wording (Kimi 2) | The doc now says a key's later position is judged against its earlier one's verdict |
| `attest` answers `Ok` with zero published on a record failure (Codex) | `Attested` gains a `refused` count, so a slot where protection withheld every signature, or could not record them, is distinguishable from a slot with nothing to publish. The refusal tests assert it |
| Keymanager ignores imported history (Codex) | That is #736 |
| Already done in 2808b51d (Kimi 3, 12) | No clone per write; compact JSON |

## Related Issues / PRs

- Follow-up: EIP-3076 interchange import/export (CLI and keymanager API), with the `eth-clients/slashing-protection-interchange-tests` v5.3.0 vectors.
- Follow-up: doppelganger protection.

## ✅ Verification Checklist

- [x] Ran `make fmt` — clean
- [x] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`) — clean
- [x] Ran `make test` (`test-consensus` plus `test-node`, at `release-fast`) — all passing

title: feat(discovery): republish the ENR's eth2 entry at fork boundaries
body:
**Draft, stacked on #732.** Pins ethrex to `80308d0d`, the head of ethrex's `feat/discv5-lock-free-local-enr`. That branch is [lambdaclass/ethrex#7488](https://github.com/lambdaclass/ethrex/pull/7488), one commit stacked on `feat/discv5-predicate-queries` (#732's pin). Not mergeable until the ethrex side is in a release and the pin goes back to a tag.

## Motivation

#732 made `/eth/v1/node/identity` read the ENR discv5 serves, but the other direction was impossible: ethrex served a private copy of the record and gave a consumer no way to edit it. So the served `eth2` entry kept the startup digest across every fork-digest boundary, and peers discovering a long-running node after one read the stale digest and rejected it.

## What this does

### 1. ethrex pin bump

ethrex's new commit makes `SharedLocalNode` the **only copy** of the served record: a lock-free `ArcSwap` slot that discovery reads on every PING/PONG/NODES/handshake, and that every writer updates by compare-and-swap.

| ethrex API | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `SharedLocalNode::load()` | Snapshot, no lock |
| `SharedLocalNode::edit_record(&signer, FnMut(&mut NodeRecordPairs))` | `NodeRecord::edit` (one `seq` bump, re-signed), swapped in by CAS; on a conflict (e.g. IP voting got in first) the edit is re-applied on the newer record |
| `DiscoveryServer::spawn(local_node, signer, ...)` | Takes the slot in place of the node, record and mirror |

`arc-swap` enters the lockfile at 1.9.2: 1.9.3 is inside the 14-day cooldown until Nov 1. `make cooldown-check` passes.

### 2. Republishing `eth2`

```text
transition::apply(epoch)
  ├─ filter.set_fork_id(fork_id, held digests)        (as before)
  └─ local_enr_writer.publish_fork_id(&fork_id)        (new)
       ├─ served eth2 == fork_id ? ── yes ──► nothing (no seq bump)
       └─ no ──► edit_record: set eth2, re-sign, seq + 1
                   └─► discv5 advertises the new seq; peers fetch the record
```

| Piece | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| When | Every `apply` call, not only on a switch. The compare makes it a no-op between boundaries, and the served entry always matches the schedule |
| No-op check | Outside the edit, since every edit bumps `seq` and a bumped `seq` sends every peer back for an identical record |
| Key ownership | `LocalEnrWriter` (crate-private) holds the slot and the node key. `LocalEnr` (read-only) is what goes to the RPC server, so the key does not |
| Retry safety | The edit only replaces `eth2` from bytes computed once, so re-running it on a newer record gives the same result |

`update_served_enr` (the warn-only stub) is gone.

## Testing

- `make lint`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked`, `make cooldown-check`
- `cargo test --workspace --profile release-fast --lib --bins`: all pass. leanSpec spec suites not run.
- New tests:
  - `a_new_fork_id_is_what_discovery_serves_next`: the edited record carries the new `eth2`, `seq` + 1, a valid signature, unchanged `attnets`/`quic`/`ip`/`udp`, and a peer on the new digest admits it
  - `republishing_the_served_fork_id_leaves_the_record_alone`: same entry, byte-identical record
  - `a_crossing_moves_the_served_eth2_entry_once`: through `transition::apply`, one edit at the boundary, none on a repeat call
- Not covered here: a remote peer fetching the edited record. ethrex's `a_consumer_edit_is_what_peers_fetch` covers that with two real discv5 nodes.

## Follow-ups

- Return the pin to an ethrex release tag.
- `syncnets` can go in the ENR now (same writer); nothing writes it yet. `beacon_wire.md` and `spec_deviations.md` now say so.
author: MegaRedHand

title: feat(validator): EIP-3076 slashing-protection import and export
body:
Stacked on #734, rebased onto its review follow-ups.

## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

#734 made slashing protection durable, but history could not move in or out. A staker migrating keys to or from ethlambda had no safe path: a key arriving from another client started as "never signed", and a key leaving got only an empty interchange from `DELETE /eth/v1/keystores`. EIP-3076's interchange format exists for exactly this, and every other client supports it.

This PR adds EIP-3076 version 5 import and export, offline through a new `ethlambda slashing-protection` command and online through the keymanager API. It also runs the shared `eth-clients/slashing-protection-interchange-tests` vectors.

## What Changed

- **`slashing_protection` (validator crate):**
  - `import`: parses a complete or minimal interchange and checks the version and `genesis_validators_root`. It then reduces each validator to its highest slot, source and target, and merges the result with the existing record by maximum, in one durable write.
    - Merging by maximum never lowers a watermark.
    - Slashable data in the file is absorbed rather than refused, as Lighthouse and Nimbus do.
    - All or nothing.
  - `export`: writes the record, or selected keys, as a minimal interchange. Keys with no record are omitted.
  - `open_offline`: opens the record without a beacon node, creating one for a given chain if there is none.
  - `interchange_chain`, `contains`, `pubkeys`, `genesis_validators_root`.
  - `file.rs`: parsing is split from reading. An import must accept a pubkey listed twice, and an attestation whose source is after its target; the vectors require both. The client's own record still refuses a duplicate pubkey.
- **`ethlambda slashing-protection import <file>` / `export [--pubkeys ...] <file>`** (`bin/ethlambda/src/slashing_protection.rs`):
  - offline, against `--validators-dir`;
  - takes the validator client's lock, so it refuses while a client runs there;
  - export refuses to overwrite an existing file.
- **Keymanager API:**
  - `POST /eth/v1/keystores` judges `slashing_protection` before touching anything: if it does not parse or is for another chain, every key in the request fails and none is loaded. It is written once the keys are saved, in the same write sequence as their registration and under the definitions lock, so a key that fails to import leaves no history behind and a concurrent `DELETE` cannot interleave.
  - `DELETE /eth/v1/keystores` returns the deleted keys' real records, replacing the deliberately empty, all-zero-root interchange.
    - The export is taken after the keys leave the store, so it covers every signature made with them.
    - A key that is gone but still has a record answers `not_active`.
- **Interop vectors:**
  - `make slashing-protection-interchange-tests` downloads v5.3.0. It is pinned, its SHA-256 is checked, and the download is stamped by version. `make test-node` depends on it.
  - `crates/validator/tests/interchange_vectors.rs` runs all 38 cases against the `should_succeed` (minimal) expectations, as Teku, Nimbus and Lodestar do.

- **An import never makes the record less strict:** every field is merged by maximum, including against existing records and repeated entries in the same file.
- **The chain must match:** an interchange for another chain is refused by the record and by the keymanager. The offline import into an empty directory creates the record for the file's chain, and the client refuses it at its next start if that is not its beacon node's chain.

On `DELETE`, the keys leave the store before the export. If the export fails, only the keys actually deleted become errors; `not_found` and malformed pubkeys keep their statuses.

title: perf(crypto): sum validated public keys through blst's batched affine addition
body:
Stack 1/4 of the BLS verification work: **(a) batched key sums** -> (b) per-block signature batch -> (c) committee key sums -> (d) index-keyed pubkey cache.

### What changed

`crates/common/crypto/src/bls.rs` only. A private helper, `sum_validated_points`, sums already-validated public keys through blst's safe `MultiPoint::add` for `[PublicKey]`, which calls `blst_p1s_add`: a batched affine addition with one shared field inversion. `fast_aggregate_verify` (now ending in `Signature::fast_aggregate_verify_pre_aggregated`) and `eth_aggregate_pubkeys` use it instead of `AggregatePublicKey::aggregate`. No `unsafe`, no signature changes. `aggregate_verify` (distinct messages) never sums keys, so it is untouched.

Notes on the helper:
- `MultiPoint::add` indexes the first element, so the empty slice is guarded (`None`). Both callers already reject empty input before.
- From 384 points up, on a host with two or more CPUs, blst splits the work over its own thread pool (separate from rayon; the same pool its pairing already ran on); below that, or on one CPU, it runs on the calling thread. The result is the same either way.
- Equal points (sync committees are drawn with replacement, so `P + P` occurs) give the same element as the sequential sum.

### Why

Measured on blst 0.3.16, block shape of 11 signature sets and 33k signers, single-threaded, on a heavily loaded M3 (ratios only; absolutes to be taken on a quiet x86 host):

| Phase per block | Ratio |
|---|---|
| key aggregation, sequential (before) | 1.4-2.5x the pairing |
| key aggregation, `blst_p1s_add` (this PR) | 1.6-2.3x faster than sequential |

### Behavior

No change: every input accepted before is accepted, every input rejected before is rejected, including the identity aggregate: `P` and `-P` are both valid keys (flip the sort flag in the compressed encoding; whoever holds `sk` can sign `-P`'s deposit with `-sk`), so a registry can hold both and an aggregate can name both. `eth_aggregate_pubkeys([P, -P])` returns the identity's bytes on both paths, and `fast_aggregate_verify` stays false because blst refuses an infinite key at pairing time.

### Tests

New unit tests compare `sum_validated_points` with `AggregatePublicKey::aggregate`: empty input, sizes 1, 2, 3, 17, 383, 384, 385, 767 and 2000, `P + P`, and runs with scattered repeats at 10, 400 and 1000 keys; `fast_aggregate_verify` with a repeated signer verifies (and fails with the key listed once); `eth_aggregate_pubkeys` equals the sequential sum with repeats; keys that cancel (adjacent `P, -P` pairs and two halves that cancel each other, at 8, 200, 400 and 1100 pairs) match the sequential sum, and `[P, -P]` aggregates to the identity and never verifies, not even against the identity signature.

Run:
- `cargo test -p ethlambda-crypto --profile release-fast --lib`: 17 passed, 14 ignored
- `cargo test -p ethlambda-state-transition --profile release-fast --lib --features beacon-spec-tests` (BLS fixture vectors): 645 passed
- `... --test beacon_spec_tests --features beacon-spec-tests -- /sync_aggregate/`: 182 passed
- `... -- /attestation/`: 356 passed
- `... -- sanity/`: 595 passed
- `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy -p ethlambda-crypto --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

Rerun after the review fixes, on the stack's tip (all four PRs, `--profile release-fast`): `ethlambda-crypto --lib` 47 passed, 14 ignored; `ethlambda-state-transition --lib --features beacon-spec-tests` (with the BLS fixture vectors) 658 passed; storage 213, blockchain 291, p2p 362, rpc 335 passed; full `beacon_spec_tests` 7493 passed, 977 ignored, 0 failed; `make lint` clean, also on a trial merge of current `main`.

title: perf(beacon): verify a block's signatures in one random-weight batch
body:
Stack 2/4 of the BLS verification work: (a) batched key sums -> **(b) per-block signature batch** -> (c) committee key sums -> (d) index-keyed pubkey cache. Based on (a).

### What changed and why

Block import checked every signature with its own pairing: the proposer's, the RANDAO reveal, each attestation, the sync aggregate and any slashings, exits and BLS changes. A pairing check is dominated by its final exponentiation, which a batch pays once for all sets.

- `ethlambda-crypto`: new `bls/batch.rs` with `SignatureSet` (`single`, `fast_aggregate`, `verify`) and `verify_signature_sets`. A set is the resolved inputs of a check (validated and summed key, message, validated signature); a batch is `verify_multiple_aggregate_signatures` with 64-bit non-zero weights from `rand`'s OS-seeded CSPRNG. Random weights are required: without them two invalid signatures can be crafted to cancel; with unpredictable 64-bit weights a forger succeeds with probability about 2^-64. A single set skips the weights. A set whose summed key is the identity fails the batch explicitly, as it fails alone.
- `ethlambda-state-transition`: new `stf/signatures.rs` with `SignatureBatch`. Operations build their set where the specification verifies it and push it with the same label the immediate check used; on a batch failure the sets are re-checked one by one and the first failing label is the rejection. Outside the crate there are only two ways to get a batch, and both check every set: `SignatureBatch::deferred(|batch| ...)` verifies once the closure returns, and `immediate()` checks at push time (see below). `new()` and `verify()` are crate-internal, so a caller cannot drop a deferring batch unverified.
- `stf::block::process_block` keeps its signature and still means "the block is valid": it runs the body inside `SignatureBatch::deferred`, so the batch is verified before it returns. `apply_block` checks the proposer's block signature on its own first, as before this PR: a block fetched by request reaches the STF without gossip's `precheck_block`, so a block its proposer never signed is still rejected after one pairing rather than after the whole body. The body's batch is verified before the state root is computed.
- The attestation validity helpers (phase0/altair, electra, gloas, payload attestations) are split into a set builder plus the existing bool function (`builder(...).is_some_and(|set| set.verify())`). Every structural check stays immediate; gossip, fork choice and block production keep calling the bool functions.

Stacked on part a (batched key sums): `SignatureSet::fast_aggregate` sums its keys with `sum_validated_points`. blst already rejects an infinity public key on both the single and the batch path; the explicit identity check in `verify_signature_sets` states that rule and changes no behavior.

### Deferred and immediate signatures

Deferred (failure rejects the block): RANDAO reveal (`block.rs`), proposer slashing headers (`operations.rs`, shared by gloas), attester slashings (phase0, electra, gloas), attestations (phase0, altair, deneb, electra, gloas), voluntary exits (phase0, deneb, electra), BLS to execution changes (`capella.rs`), sync aggregate (`altair.rs`; empty participants keep the infinity-signature rule and push nothing), gloas execution payload bid, gloas payload attestations.

Immediate, unchanged (failure changes state but does not reject): every deposit signature (`operations.rs`, `electra.rs`, `epoch/electra.rs`) and the gloas builder deposit signature. The gloas envelope signature is not reachable from `process_block`.

### Behavior notes

- Every accepted input is still accepted and every rejected one rejected. A rejected block now reports the first failing signature's label, but another defect later in the block may be reported first or instead; the label of a bad signature is the one the immediate check used.
- An `Err` now can leave the state partly mutated by operations whose signature was checked at the end. Import runs the transition on a clone (`transition_block`, `fork_choice.rs`) and every caller discards the state after an error.
- The operation packer in block production applies candidates in place and relies on a rejected candidate writing nothing. It therefore passes `SignatureBatch::immediate()`, which checks at push time and keeps that guarantee.
- `gloas::process_block_and_verify` is the helper for the direct gloas drivers in block production.

Immediate, as on `main`: the proposer's block signature (`apply_block`), so a forged block stays cheap to reject.

### Measured

On a loaded M3, the pairing per block took 2.7-4x less wall time with one batch. That ratio mixes two effects: fewer final exponentiations, and blst's `verify_multiple_aggregate_signatures` spreading the Miller loops over its own pool where the old per-set check used one worker. CPU time drops too: profiling a Hoodi block replay on a Ryzen 9700X (the whole stack, warm caches) puts pairing and hash-to-curve at 7.9 ms CPU per block before and 2.4 ms after. That run predates this PR's review fix, which takes the proposer's signature back out of the batch, so it now costs about one more pairing per block than measured.

### Tests

- `cargo test -p ethlambda-crypto --profile release-fast --lib`: the batch tests cover a valid batch of ten, one bad among ten, swapped signatures, empty batch, single set, repeated messages, mixed single and aggregate, agreement with `bls::verify` and `bls::fast_aggregate_verify`, `None` for invalid inputs, weights never zero, an infinity signature among valid sets, and keys that cancel (`[P, -P]` never verifies, alone or in a batch, with the identity signature or a real one; `[P, P, -P]` verifies under `P`'s signature).
- `cargo test -p ethlambda-state-transition --profile release-fast --lib --features beacon-spec-tests`: 655 passed, 0 failed, rerun after the merge (includes the BLS fixture vectors and the new tests: a bad RANDAO reveal is deferred and rejected by the batch, a valid one passes, `RandaoVerification::Skip` pushes nothing, deferred and immediate failures carry the same label, one bad signature among several rejects the batch).
- `cargo test -p ethlambda-state-transition --profile release-fast --test beacon_spec_tests --features beacon-spec-tests` (unfiltered, mainnet preset): 7493 passed, 0 failed, 977 ignored. The operation runner builds a batch around each operation and treats an `Err` from `verify()` as the rejection.
- Filtered `beacon_spec_tests` after the merge: `/attestation/` 356 passed, `/sync_aggregate/` 182 passed, `sanity/` 595 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --profile release-fast -p ethlambda-crypto -p ethlambda-state-transition -p ethlambda-rpc --all-targets -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --all` applied.

On this branch after its review fixes: crypto `--lib` 32 passed; state-transition `--lib` 655 passed; `beacon_spec_tests` `operations/` 2141, `sanity/` 595, `finality/` 41, `fork_choice/` 206, `random/` 1969 (175 ignored), `transition/` 172, `sync/` 6 passed; the rpc validator-client tests pass.

Rerun after the review fixes, on the stack's tip (all four PRs, `--profile release-fast`): `ethlambda-crypto --lib` 47 passed, 14 ignored; `ethlambda-state-transition --lib --features beacon-spec-tests` (with the BLS fixture vectors) 658 passed; storage 213, blockchain 291, p2p 362, rpc 335 passed; full `beacon_spec_tests` 7493 passed, 977 ignored, 0 failed; `make lint` clean, also on a trial merge of current `main`.

title: fix(p2p): disconnect peers whose gossipsub send queue never drains
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

A heap profile of our mainnet follower (2.8 GB steady RSS) showed about 490 MB of gossipsub message copies that never went away: they sat in the send queues of a few peers whose gossipsub connection handler had disabled itself.

The mechanism, in the pinned rust-libp2p (same in upstream master):

- The handler counts every inbound and outbound substream event, successful ones included, and after `MAX_SUBSTREAM_ATTEMPTS` sets itself to `Disabled(MaxSubstreamAttempts)`. In that state `poll` is `Pending` forever, so the send queue is never read again.
- The behaviour is not told. It keeps queueing forwards for the peer until the per-peer queue is full.
- A queued message is only dropped when the handler takes it off the queue, so the copies stay in memory until the connection closes. Other protocols keep using that connection, so nothing closes it.

Gossipsub does report such a peer: `Event::SlowPeer` every heartbeat. We dropped that event. Gossipsub's own score penalty for it (`slow_peer_weight`) left the peer in the `negative` band, nowhere near the graylist. Lighthouse handles the event in its peer manager instead.

## What Changed

- `crates/net/p2p/src/swarm_adapter.rs`:
  - `SlowPeers` collects `SlowPeer` reports between the existing 10 s checks.
  - `disconnect_slow_peers` runs on that tick, right after `disconnect_graylisted_peers`. It disconnects a peer reported in each of the last `SLOW_PEER_CHECK_LIMIT` (6) checks, so about a minute without a break.
  - The event is still forwarded to the P2P actor as before.
- `crates/net/p2p/src/metrics.rs`: adds the `lean_gossipsub_slow_peer_disconnects_total` counter.
- `docs/beacon_wire.md`, `docs/metrics.md`, `CLAUDE.md`: describe the rule and the metric.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- **Beacon only.** The gate is the one the graylist check already uses: peer scoring on. Lean is unchanged.
- **Only a persistent failure disconnects.** A check with no report resets the peer's streak, so a peer that is briefly slow keeps its connection.
- **Known gap:** some peers keep their pinned queue until the connection closes, as today. These are peers whose handler is dead but whose failures stop within the minute, for example once they are pruned from the mesh and score below the gossip threshold.
- Since #719 caps `libp2p_gossipsub` logs at ERROR, gossipsub's "Send Queue full" WARNs no longer show by default. An operator now sees these peers through this change's `info!` disconnect line and the new counter.

## Tests Added / Run

- Four unit tests on `SlowPeers`:
  - a peer failing in every check is returned at the limit;
  - a quiet check resets the streak;
  - several reports in one check count once;
  - a returned peer starts a new streak.
- Replayed the follower's log in 10 s bins:
  - The three stuck peers had unbroken runs of "Send Queue full" of 29, 54 and 377 bins (5 to 63 minutes), so each would have been disconnected within about a minute.
  - A peer with 3 isolated failures would have kept its connection.
- `cargo test --profile release-fast -p ethlambda-p2p --lib`: 366 passed.

## Related Issues / PRs

- One of three memory fixes from the same profile; the other two are separate PRs (vote-table growth, state encoding).

## ✅ Verification Checklist

- [x] Ran `make fmt` — clean
- [ ] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`) — clean. Ran `cargo clippy --locked -p ethlambda-p2p --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean), not the full workspace target
- [ ] Ran `make test` (`test-consensus` plus `test-node`, at `release-fast`) — all passing. Ran only the p2p lib tests above

title: fix(storage): grow the beacon vote table exactly instead of doubling
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

`Store::latest_messages` (the beacon fork choice's latest vote per validator) is a dense table indexed by validator index. `set_latest_message` grew it with `resize`, which at least doubles the capacity whenever an index lands past it. A registry that keeps gaining validators crosses that edge soon after the table is first sized. So on our mainnet follower the table had room for about twice the registry, and roughly half of its 256 MB (heap profile) was never used.

## What Changed

- `crates/storage/src/store.rs`: when a new index is past the capacity, `set_latest_message` now calls `reserve_exact` for that index plus `LATEST_MESSAGES_HEADROOM` (4096) spare entries, then `resize`s as before.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- Same contents and indexing; only the allocation size changes.
- A registry growing by a few validators an epoch still reallocates rarely, once per headroom's worth of new indices.
- Expected saving on the mainnet follower: about 120 MB.

## Tests Added / Run

- `the_latest_message_table_grows_exactly_rather_than_doubling` checks three things:
  - the first index sizes the table to at most that index plus the headroom;
  - a nearby index leaves the capacity unchanged;
  - an index past the headroom grows the table to less than twice its previous size.
- `cargo test --profile release-fast -p ethlambda-storage --lib`: 211 passed.

## Related Issues / PRs

title: fix(types): encode a beacon state without holding it twice
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

libssz's container encoder writes each fixed-size field past the end of the buffer and then moves it into place, and its `to_ssz` reserves only the encoding's length. So when a state's last field is fixed-size, encoding it reallocates a buffer the size of the whole state to twice that, copying it, just for that last field. Fulu's state ends on `proposer_lookahead`, gloas's on `ptc_window`. A 44 MB fulu state encoded with plain `to_ssz` ended in an 88 MB buffer.

On a mainnet state (hundreds of MB) that is one extra state-sized copy per encode. Two places pay it:

- **The state writer**, on every import. `encode_state_value` encoded the state, then copied it into a second buffer behind its fork tag.
- **The Beacon API's SSZ state response**, `/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/{state_id}`, on every request.

## What Changed

- `crates/common/types/src/beacon/containers/mod.rs`:
  - `BeaconState::ssz_append_capacity()`: the encoding's length plus the largest fixed-size field of any fork's state.
  - `BeaconState::ssz_append(buf)` appends the encoding to a caller's buffer.
  - `BeaconState::to_ssz()` now appends into a buffer with that capacity instead of calling libssz's `to_ssz`. That fixes every caller of the enum, the API response included.
- `crates/storage/src/state_codec.rs`: `encode_state_value` pushes the fork tag, then appends the state into the same buffer, sized `1 + ssz_append_capacity()`.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- Same bytes as before; only the allocation changes. Both tests compare against libssz's own per-fork encoding.
- The headroom is the largest fixed-size field (`randao_mixes` on mainnet, 2 MiB; `ptc_window` on minimal). Any fixed-size field can then be written past the end, wherever it sits in the container. So the bound holds for every fork, including the earlier ones whose state also ends on a fixed-size field (phase0's `finalized_checkpoint`, altair's `next_sync_committee`).
- The returned `Vec` carries that headroom as spare capacity: a few MiB at most, next to a state of hundreds of MB.
- Callers that encode a per-fork struct directly still go through libssz's `to_ssz`. I found none outside tests.

## Tests Added / Run

- `ssz_append_never_regrows_a_buffer_with_its_capacity_to_spare` (fulu and gloas): `ssz_append` and `to_ssz` both match libssz's encoding, and neither changes the buffer's capacity.
- `a_beacon_state_value_is_its_tag_then_its_ssz_in_one_buffer`: the tag byte, then the state's SSZ, in one buffer of exactly the reserved capacity. The value round-trips through `decode_state_value`.
- `cargo test --profile release-fast -p ethlambda-types -p ethlambda-storage -p ethlambda-rpc --lib`: 233, 211 and 335 passed.

## Related Issues / PRs

- One of three memory fixes from the same profile: #739 (slow gossipsub peers), #740 (vote-table growth).

title: perf(beacon): verify attestations against committee key sums
body:
Stack 3/4 of the BLS verification work: (a) batched key sums -> (b) per-block signature batch -> **(c) committee key sums** -> (d) index-keyed pubkey cache. Based on (b).

An attestation aggregate usually covers most of its committee, and its verification key is the sum of the attesters' keys. This PR precomputes each committee's key sum once per shuffling, off the import path, and derives an attestation's key as `committee_sum - sum(non-attesters)` when more than half the committee attested, and as `sum(attesters)` otherwise. The group element is the same either way, so the pairing check is unchanged; only the number of point additions differs (absentees instead of attesters).

### What it changes on top of the signature batch

- `ethlambda-crypto`
  - `bls/committee_sums.rs`: `AggregatePubkey` (`sum`, `minus`, `plus`, `verify`) and `CommitteeKeySums`. Negation uses blst's safe `sub_aggregate`, so there is no `unsafe`.
  - `SignatureSet::from_aggregate(key, message, signature)`: builds a set from an already-summed key (`None` when the signature fails `sig_validate`; one affine conversion of the key). `AggregatePubkey::verify` delegates to it, so both checks share one path, and the batch's identity-key guard covers it.
  - One projective sum helper in `bls.rs` (`sum_validated_projective`); the batched-key-sum PR's `sum_validated_points` is now a thin wrapper that converts to affine once. Committee sums add and subtract projective points, so building them on the affine helper would cost an extra field inversion per committee, about 512 per block.
- `ethlambda-storage`: each resident shuffling gets a second `OnceLock<Arc<CommitteeKeySums>>` beside its committees, so eviction and head pinning stay in one place and the sums die with their shuffling. `resident_key_sums` is lookup only; `get_or_init_key_sums` builds into a resident entry and never holds the entry-list lock while building.
- `ethlambda-state-transition`
  - `CommitteeCacheExt::key_sums` (lookup only: import never builds) and `warm_key_sums` (one `iter_validators()` pass, then rayon across committees). A committee with an invalid member key gets no sum and falls back to the direct path.
  - `attesters_aggregate_pubkey` (`helpers/electra.rs`), with the majority rule, usable by gloas through the same `is_set` closure as `attesting_indices_from_committee_bits`. Committees derived from their sums are added one by one; the attesters of every committee summed directly go into one sum. With cold sums that is the single sum over every attester that #738 makes, at its cost: one sum per committee would pay blst's pool dispatch once per committee for a few hundred keys each, which made the cold path slower than #738's.
  - Electra, fulu and gloas `process_attestation` build their `SignatureSet` from it (`electra_attestation_signature_set`, `gloas_attestation_signature_set`). The indexed attestation is still built, for the participation flags, and the same structural checks are made on it (non-empty, sorted and unique; gloas's `MAX_VALIDATORS_PER_SLOT` bound). Same signing root, same push label. Phase0 through deneb are unchanged.
- `ethlambda-blockchain` (`epoch_precompute.rs`): the precomputed state is sent to the actor first, then the sums are warmed in the same blocking task, so the epoch's first block never waits for them. The task warms the epoch's sums and the previous epoch's (for the attestations its blocks carry from it), so a restart mid-epoch or a boundary whose worker did not run is covered at the next one. When the boundary state is already cached (a gloas bid for the epoch's first slot advances it), no worker runs, so a warm-only task runs from that state instead. Warming is skipped before electra, whose attestations never read the sums. New histogram `lean_beacon_committee_key_sums_warm_seconds` (in `docs/metrics.md`), recorded only when sums are actually built and covering the sums alone.

### Soundness of keying sums by `ShufflingKey`

The sums are filed under (epoch, decision root), so two states with one key must agree on each member's public key as well as on who the members are. Checked against this repo's spec code:

- The registry is append-only (`process_deposit`, electra's pending-deposit path); a validator's index and pubkey are fixed at append and no code assigns `pubkey` afterwards.
- A new validator is appended with `activation_epoch = FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH`. Only `process_registry_updates` (epoch processing at epoch N) assigns one, `compute_activation_exit_epoch(N) = N + 1 + MAX_SEED_LOOKAHEAD`.
- A member of epoch E's committees is active at E, so it was activated at some N <= E - 1 - MAX_SEED_LOOKAHEAD, and appended no later. That precedes the end of E - 2, so the decision-root block already has it at that index with that key, and every descendant inherits it.

The argument is in the `CommitteeCacheExt::key_sums` doc comment.

### Measured

On a heavily loaded M3, blst 0.3.16, **single-threaded**, block shape of 11 signature sets and 33k signers:

| Phase per block | Ratio |
|---|---|
| key aggregation, sequential (before the batched sums) | 1.4-2.5x the pairing |
| key aggregation, 5% missed only | 20-40x less (realistic ~10x) |

The single-threaded ratio overstates the wall-time gain on a multi-core host, where #738's one large sum already runs on blst's pool. In CPU time, profiling a Hoodi block replay on a Ryzen 9700X (the whole stack, warm sums) puts key summation at 12.3 ms CPU per block before the stack and 1.5 ms after.

### Behavior notes

- Accepted and rejected inputs are unchanged. Cold sums, an evicted shuffling or an invalid member key all take the direct sum of the attesters; a bad signature is rejected under the same label, warm or cold.
- The sync aggregate is not covered: its keys come from `current_sync_committee.pubkeys`, which has no committee sums.
- Warming builds the epoch's committees if they are not resident, and copies every validator's 48-byte key once: roughly 115 MB transient at 2.4M validators, on the blocking worker. It runs on rayon's global pool (and blst's, for each committee's sum), so it shares cores with import; the first warm-up after a start also validates every active key.
- Import never builds sums. With cold sums (while syncing, when no precompute runs, or before the first warm-up after a start) attestations take the direct path, at #738's cost.

### Tests

New tests:
- crypto: compressed-byte equality of `sum`/`minus`/`plus` against blst's direct sum (including duplicate keys, and `minus` over 40 random masks of a 64-key committee); `verify` against `bls::fast_aggregate_verify` with real signatures; the identity aggregate rejected; the empty and invalid-key cases.
- storage: `key_sums` never builds or inserts; sums are built once into a resident shuffling only; sums are evicted with their shuffling.
- state-transition: random masks (empty, one bit, below half, exactly half, half plus one, all, random) over one and two committees, cold and warm, checked by verifying the aggregate of the attesters' real signatures; invalid-member fallback; a block-level test with warm sums where a good attestation gives the same post-state root warm and cold and a bad signature is rejected with the attestation label either way.
- spec runners: every electra-or-later `operations/*/attestation` case and every block run (`sanity`, `finality`, `random`) now runs twice, cold and after `warm_key_sums` (previous, current and next epoch of the state each block applies to); both runs must reach the same verdict and post-state.

title: perf(crypto): resolve registry public keys through a validator-index table
body:
Stack 4/4 of the BLS verification work: (a) batched key sums -> (b) per-block signature batch -> (c) committee key sums -> **(d) index-keyed pubkey cache**. Based on (c).

### What changed

- `IndexedPubkey { index, pubkey }` and a sealed trait `PubkeySource`, implemented for `BlsPubkey` (byte path) and `IndexedPubkey` (index path). `verify`, `fast_aggregate_verify`, `eth_fast_aggregate_verify`, `key_validate`, `eth_aggregate_pubkeys`, `SignatureSet::single`, `SignatureSet::fast_aggregate`, `AggregatePubkey::sum` and `AggregatePubkey::minus` are generic over it, so existing `&[BlsPubkey]` callers compile unchanged. (`aggregate_verify` stays byte-only: no caller knows indices there.)
- `PubkeyCache` gains an index table: lazily allocated chunks of 4096 `OnceLock<(BlsPubkey, PublicKey)>`, bounded by the existing `MAX_CACHED_PUBKEYS`. Reads take no lock and no hash. Entries are set once; the first writer wins.
- A lookup hits the table only when the stored bytes equal the bytes the caller read from its state. A mismatch, an empty slot, or an index past the bound goes to the byte-keyed map. A key resolved by index is stored in the table, not the map. A key that loses the race for its slot goes to the map. A key first validated through the byte path and later looked up by index is copied into its empty slot (set-once, first writer wins) and also stays in the map, since byte-path callers cannot see the table and would otherwise validate it again. Such a key is held twice, which is why every caller that reads a key from the registry by index passes the index (gossip included, below). Invalid keys are cached in neither structure.
- The module documentation's keying paragraph now covers both structures and why the byte comparison keeps the argument for byte keys: an index names whatever key the caller's state says, so it is never trusted alone.
- Call sites switched to `IndexedPubkey`:
  - state transition: the three `indexed_attestation_signature_set_with_domain` builders, `indexed_payload_attestation_signature_set`, `attesters_aggregate_pubkey` (and so `attestation_signature_set`), `warm_key_sums`, randao, the proposer block signature, proposer slashing headers, and voluntary exits (phase0, deneb, electra);
  - gossip: aggregator selection proof and signature, subnet attestations, data column sidecar headers, voluntary exits, proposer slashings, payload attestations, proposer preferences, sync committee messages and contribution aggregators, and the block precheck;
  - Beacon API: submitted attestations and the gloas proposal's RANDAO reveal check.
- Left on the byte path: deposits, BLS-to-execution changes (`from_bls_pubkey` is not a registry key), the sync aggregate and sync contributions (keys come from the sync committee's own key list), gloas builder keys (builder registry, not validator).
- Metrics: `lean_beacon_pubkey_cache_entries` gains a `structure` label (`map`, `table`), and the new `lean_beacon_pubkey_cache_index_chunks` counts allocated table chunks, which is what the table's memory follows.

### Why

Pubkey lookups through the sharded SipHash map cost 0.5-0.7x of the block's pairing (measured on a heavily loaded M3, ratios only; absolutes to be taken on a quiet x86 host). The index table replaces hash + read lock + probe with one array read and a 48-byte compare.

### Memory

| | Payload | Overhead | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Byte map (hashbrown) | 48 + 96 = 144 B | 1 control byte per bucket, load factor 7/8 at most | per key held: 166 B at the 7/8 peak, up to 331 B just after a resize |
| Index table | 144 B | `Once` state, padded to alignment 8 | 152 B per registry index, filled or not |

The table's cost follows the registry's index span, not the number of keys in it: a chunk is allocated whole on its first key, and exited validators are spread through every chunk. On a registry of about 2.4M indices with about 1.2M active, every chunk is allocated, about 350 MiB, against about 290 MiB for the map holding the active keys on the parent branch: about +57 MiB. If that is too much, slots holding a pointer to a boxed entry would cut the empty slots to 16 B (about 230 MiB in total) at the price of one pointer chase per hit.

An earlier revision of this PR left gossip on the byte path. Gossip then validated every key import had already put in the table a second time and held it in both structures, so the map refilled with nearly every active key within about a day, about doubling the cache. Every registry read now passes its index.

### Behavior notes

No input accepted before is rejected or the other way round. Spec fixtures reuse indices with different keys across states in one process, so the full spec run exercises the mismatch fallback continuously.

### Tests

- `cargo test -p ethlambda-crypto --profile release-fast --lib` (new: a byte-path key is copied into the table on its first index lookup, hit after warm and not in the map, different key at a warmed index falls back and verifies, index past the bound, a cold lookup allocates nothing, invalid keys cached nowhere, concurrent readers and writers agree with `key_validate`).
- `cargo test -p ethlambda-state-transition --profile release-fast --lib --features beacon-spec-tests`: 658 passed.
- `beacon_spec_tests` filters: `/attestation/` 356, `/sync_aggregate/` 182, `sanity/` 595, `random/` 1969 passed (175 ignored); full unfiltered: 7493 passed, 977 ignored, 0 failed.
- `cargo fmt --all`; clippy `-D warnings` clean on `ethlambda-crypto` and `ethlambda-state-transition`.
- `cargo clippy --profile release-fast --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (rpc, p2p and blockchain compile against the generic signatures).

Rerun after the review fixes, on the stack's tip (all four PRs, `--profile release-fast`): `ethlambda-crypto --lib` 47 passed, 14 ignored; `ethlambda-state-transition --lib --features beacon-spec-tests` (with the BLS fixture vectors) 658 passed; storage 213, blockchain 291, p2p 362, rpc 335 passed; full `beacon_spec_tests` 7493 passed, 977 ignored, 0 failed; `make lint` clean, also on a trial merge of current `main`.

title: fix(rpc): end event streams when the node shuts down
body:
## Motivation

Graceful shutdown waits for every in-flight response, and an SSE stream never finishes on its own: the router keeps its own `EventBus` clone, so the broadcast channel never closes and `RecvError::Closed` never arrives. Any subscriber left connected to `/eth/v1/events` or `/lean/v0/events` therefore holds SIGINT forever (SIGKILL skips the state flush).

This blocks running a permanent subscriber next to a node, such as ethPandaOps' contributoor, which keeps one stream per topic open and reconnects on its own.

## Changes

- `serve()` hands each router its shutdown token as a `ShutdownSignal` extension.
- `sse_response` ends the stream with `take_until` when the signal fires. Both the lean and the Beacon API handlers pass it through.
- `docs/rpc.md`: streams end at shutdown.

## Tests

- `events_stream_ends_when_the_server_shuts_down`: the body completes once the signal is cancelled while the bus stays open.
- `a_connected_event_stream_does_not_hold_up_shutdown` (`tests/http_servers.rs`): binds a real socket, keeps `/eth/v1/events` open, cancels, and expects the server to stop within 5 s. Verified to fail (time out) without the fix.

title: perf(fork_choice): build the parent-to-children map once in get_filtered_block_tree
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation
`filter_block_tree` found a block's children by scanning the whole block index
(`Store::block_index`, the full `LiveChain` window since the finalized block) at
every node it visited. The recursion visits every node of the justified subtree,
so the head walk was quadratic in the number of unfinalized blocks. That runs on
every block import and every tick through `get_head`, and the cost grows exactly
when the node is under pressure: a finality stall or a range catch-up from a
checkpoint anchor.

`walk_head` and `invalidate_subtree` already build a parent-to-children map once
per call; this brings the filter in line with them. Found by Kimi during an
improvement review.

## What Changed
- `crates/blockchain/state_transition/src/beacon/fork_choice.rs`
  - `get_filtered_block_tree` builds `HashMap<Root, Vec<Root>>` from the index in
    one pass and hands it down.
  - `filter_block_tree` takes that map and does one lookup per node instead of a
    scan per node.
  - Rustdoc that described the per-node scan is updated (the module's "never needs
    a `BTreeMap`" section, the `filter_block_tree` doc, one cross-reference in
    `compute_head`).

`compute_head` and `get_node_children` keep their per-level scans on purpose:
they are the spec-literal references the tests compare the walk against.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees
- The filtered tree is identical: child order only ORs viability and inserts
  into a map, so it cannot change the result.
- No storage change, no change to any signature the node or the spec harness
  calls (`filter_block_tree` is `pub` but has no callers outside this file).
- Cost goes from O(N × M) to O(N), N the live window and M the justified subtree.

## Tests Added / Run
- New: `the_filtered_tree_matches_the_spec_literal_children_scan_on_random_trees`
  keeps the old scan as a reference and asserts the map-based result equals it on
  100 random trees, including slots where a branch is filtered out (asserts that
  happened at least once, so it cannot pass vacuously).
- Existing: the randomized differential test and the fork-choice fixture suite
  already cover `get_filtered_block_tree`.
- Ran: `make fmt`, `make lint`, fork_choice unit tests (94 passed), mainnet
  fork-choice fixture cases (206 passed), `make test-consensus` (1324 passed).

## Related Issues / PRs
- None

## ✅ Verification Checklist
- [x] Ran `make fmt` — clean
- [x] Ran `make lint` (clippy with `-D warnings`) — clean
- [ ] Ran `make test` — `test-consensus` run locally; `test-node` left to CI
      (unrelated to this change)

title: feat(rpc): serve /eth/v1/node/peers, /peers/{peer_id} and /peer_count
body:
## Summary

Serves the Beacon API's `GET /eth/v1/node/peers`, `GET /eth/v1/node/peers/{peer_id}` and `GET /eth/v1/node/peer_count`. ethPandaOps' contributoor (xatu sentry) polls `/peers` every minute and got a 404.

## Design notes

- `ethlambda-network-api` gains `PeerTableController` (`Arc<RwLock<HashMap>>`), `ConnectedPeer` and `PeerDirection`, mirroring `MetaDataController`. Strings only, so the crate stays free of libp2p types.
- The p2p actor is the sole writer: insert on `ConnectionEstablished` with `num_established == 1`, remove on `ConnectionClosed` with `num_established == 0`. RPC reads it at request time via a new `BeaconIdentity.peers: Option<PeerTableController>`; absent means an empty list.
- Only connected peers are tracked, so `state` is always `connected`. A `state` filter for another valid state returns an empty list, and `peer_count` reports `"0"` for the other states. Documented in `docs/rpc.md`.
- `last_seen_p2p_address` is the first connection's remote address, with `/p2p/<peer id>` appended if absent. `direction` is the first connection's, as in `connected_peers`.
- `enr`: `DiscoveredPeer` now carries the record's `enr:` string; the dial loop keeps it per peer (`peer_enrs`, dropped in `forget_discovered_peer`) and it is read at connect. `null` for inbound peers and `--bootnodes` dials. No new network requests.
- Also: `state`/`direction` accept repeated and comma-separated values (values of one parameter are alternatives, parameters are AND-combined); peers are sorted by peer id for stable output; `/peers/{peer_id}` validates the id as non-empty base58 (the RPC crate has no libp2p), so a malformed id is a 400 and a well-formed unknown one a 404.
- Lean surface (`/lean/v0`) untouched.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p ethlambda-network-api -p ethlambda-p2p -p ethlambda-rpc -p ethlambda --all-targets --profile release-fast -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p ethlambda-rpc --profile release-fast --lib -- beacon::node` (15 passed): list, state/direction/both filters, invalid value 400, `meta.count`, null ENR, `/peers/{id}` hit/miss/malformed, `peer_count` quoting, absent table
- [x] `cargo test -p ethlambda-network-api --profile release-fast --lib` (3 passed)
- [ ] The p2p write path has no test of its own; check it on a running node with `curl :5052/eth/v1/node/peers`

title: feat(rpc): emit gloas events and head_v2 on /eth/v1/events
body:
## Summary

`GET /eth/v1/events` accepted every gloas topic but emitted none of them, so contributoor (ethPandaOps) had nothing to show for our nodes on Sepolia. This emits:

| Topic | Emitted when |
|---|---|
| `head_v2` | next to every `head` (pre-gloas with `payload_status: "full"`), and again for the same block on an empty -> full payload status change |
| `block` | unchanged, plus `builder_index` and `block_hash` for gloas blocks (absent before) |
| `execution_payload`, `execution_payload_available` | the chain actor imports an envelope |
| `execution_payload_gossip` | an envelope passes gossip validation, or `POST /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes` accepts it |
| `execution_payload_bid`, `proposer_preferences`, `payload_attestation_message` | passes gossip validation, or the matching `POST` accepts it |

`head` is deprecated by the specification in favour of `head_v2` and is still emitted. `docs/rpc.md` has the new rows, drops the stale "this build stops at fulu" sentence, and documents the `execution_payload_available` timing.

## Design notes

- **Publisher.** Bids, preferences and payload attestation messages are validated in `ethlambda-p2p` and never reach the chain actor, and p2p does not depend on `ethlambda-blockchain` (which owns `EventBus`). So `ethlambda-network-api` gets a `GossipEventSink` trait and a `GossipEvent` enum, `EventBus` implements the trait, and `main.rs` passes `Some(Arc::new(events.clone()))` into `P2P::spawn` (new last parameter). The p2p side is one function, `publish_gossip_event`, called from `Validated::forward` on `Accept` only, behind `has_subscribers()`. The API handlers already run next to the bus, so they emit directly through a small `emit_accepted` helper; the bus is an `Option<Extension<EventBus>>` there so routers built without one (the handlers' own tests) still serve.
- **Envelope gossip: sink, not `BlockAnnouncement`.** Accepted gossip envelopes do reach the actor, but `new_execution_payload_envelope` carries no accepted-versus-queued flag, and gossip also forwards `Queue`d envelopes through it. Following the `block_gossip` pattern would have meant a new parameter on that trait method and every implementor and test double. The sink already exists for the other three, takes `Accept` only, and touches one function.
- **`execution_payload_available`.** Emitted right after `execution_payload`, from the same import. The actor imports an envelope only once the payload is verified and every sampled column is stored, which is what the event reports, so there is no later moment to wait for.
- **`head_v2` dependent roots.** `current_epoch_dependent_root` is the root at `start_slot(epoch - 1) - 1` and `next_epoch_dependent_root` the root at `start_slot(epoch) - 1`, genesis root on underflow. These are `head`'s `previous_duty_dependent_root` and `current_duty_dependent_root` renamed, so they come from the same `NewChain::dependent_root`.
- **`payload_status`.** `full` for every pre-gloas head. From gloas on it follows `Store::head_payload_status`, with `empty` when none is recorded yet. The re-emission is driven by the `EventView` (the head and its recorded status as last reported), so it fires once per empty -> full transition and nothing else repeats (full -> empty is optional in the specification and left out). Both `head_v2` emissions keep the 32-slot recency gate `head` has.
- **`version`** on `head_v2` is the head state's fork; the bid, message and preferences wrappers are always `gloas`.
- **`block` fields** are `Option`s with `skip_serializing_if`, so a pre-gloas block's JSON is byte-identical to before.
- A `head` move now puts two beacon events on the shared ring instead of one. The existing head tests read through `drain`, which leaves `head_v2` out; the new ones use `drain_all`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p ethlambda-network-api -p ethlambda-blockchain -p ethlambda-p2p -p ethlambda-rpc -p ethlambda --all-targets --profile release-fast -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p ethlambda-blockchain --profile release-fast --lib -- events`: JSON shape of every new payload against the specification examples (field names, quoting, `version` wrapper), the sink-to-topic mapping, the `payload_status` label.
- [x] `cargo test -p ethlambda-blockchain --profile release-fast --lib -- head_v2 imported_envelope block_event_carries ...` and the existing beacon event tests: `head_v2` dependent roots across epochs 0 to 2 including underflow, the pre-gloas `full`, the empty -> full re-emission (and that full -> empty and a repeat do not re-emit), `publish_envelope_imported`, and the `block` event's bid fields.
- [x] `cargo test -p ethlambda-rpc --profile release-fast --lib -- beacon::`: an accepted bid and accepted preferences are announced once in their wrapper, a refused or already-pooled bid is not.
- [x] `cargo test -p ethlambda-blockchain --profile release-fast --features beacon-spec-tests --lib -- beacon_envelope` against the v1.7.0-beta.2 fixtures: 47 passed, including `an_imported_envelope_emits_execution_payload_then_available`, which drives the actor's real envelope import.
- Not covered by a test: the p2p `publish_gossip_event` function, and the payload attestation and envelope POST handlers' emission (same helper as the bid and preferences handlers).

title: feat(beacon): fast confirmation rule, its event and the engine safe hash
body:
## Summary

- Implements the Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR) for the beacon follower: `beacon::fast_confirmation` in `ethlambda-state-transition`, one Rust function per spec function, named as the spec names it.
- The actor runs it once per slot and publishes the Beacon API `fast_confirmation` event (`{"block", "slot", "current_slot"}`, integers quoted) after every run, changed or not.
- `forkchoiceUpdated`'s `safe` hash is now the spec's `get_safe_execution_block_hash` (the confirmed block's payload hash; gloas: its bid's `parent_block_hash`), replacing the justified-checkpoint stand-in. The matching deviation in `docs/spec_deviations.md` is gone.
- contributoor (ethPandaOps) subscribes to this event; before this the node accepted the topic and never sent it.
- **Review focus:** the `safe` hash the EL receives now comes from this rule, and no consensus-specs fixtures exist for it, only the hand-ported scenarios listed below. It also has not been profiled on a mainnet-size state yet (see the unchecked test-plan item).

## Design notes

**Spec commit.** consensus-specs `master` at `f993cf2`, recorded in the module doc, not the pinned `v1.7.0-beta.2` (no FCR fixtures exist there, so nothing ties us to it). Since beta.2 master fixed the gloas empty-slot support discount (#5672), made committee weight precise (#5670), added the restart-resilient confirmed root (#5673) and asserts `support_discount <= maximum_support` (#5788). A later bump should diff `phase0`, `bellatrix` and `gloas` `fast-confirmation.md` against that commit.

**Where state lives.** The six variables of `FastConfirmationStore` (not a copy of the fork-choice store) are `FastConfirmationVariables` in `ethlambda-types`, held in the `Store`'s `BeaconScratch` next to the other in-memory fork-choice extras (`Store::fast_confirmation`). `FastConfirmationStore` in the new module is the spec's store: a borrowed `Store` plus those variables, plus a per-run memo. Initialization is lazy and equals `get_fast_confirmation_store`: the first run of a process, or the first after a reset, starts every variable at the finalized checkpoint. Only `confirmed_root` is persisted (`Metadata["beacon_fast_confirmed_root"]`, written when it changes; no `DB_VERSION` bump, an older directory just has no row). The first synced run of a process offers that row to `get_restart_resilient_confirmed_root` (the spec's implementation-defined `get_root_confirmed_before_restart`), once.

**When it runs.** In the beacon actor's per-slot tick (`recompute_beacon_head_with(true)`): after the store clock advance, the deferred aggregates (so attestations from past slots are applied) and the head recompute, and before `forkchoiceUpdated`, so that call carries this slot's safe block. Not on block imports, which recompute the head many times a slot: the spec requires `update_fast_confirmation_variables` exactly once per slot, before `get_attestation_due_ms`.

**Sync gating.** Same staleness gate as the `head` event: the run is skipped while the head is more than `HEAD_EVENT_RECENCY_SLOTS` (32) behind the wall clock, and the variables are reset to the finalized checkpoint, since the rule assumes synchrony from the start of the previous slot and the stored heads would be stale and eventually pruned. It is also skipped when the head recompute failed. A failing run logs a warning, publishes nothing and leaves the variables as they were.

**Complexity per run.** `O(V + M + B log B)` plus committee-range work, for `V` validators, `M` latest messages, `B` unfinalized blocks. The spec's helpers each walk the registry or the committees and are called once per block of the confirmed chain (up to ~64 blocks), which at ~1M validators would be tens of passes per slot. Instead, per run:
- one pass over each balance source's registry (at most three: previous and current observed justified checkpoint, pulled-up head state), producing active and unslashed balance arrays;
- one bottom-up fold of the latest messages into every block's `get_attestation_score` (as `compute_weights` does for the head), instead of one scan per block;
- a memoized committee weight per `(source, slot)`, so a range inside one epoch is a sum of slots; only ranges that cross an epoch boundary without covering an epoch, and empty-slot support ranges, deduplicate validators (a bitmap over the range's committees);
- committees from the store's shared committee cache; `get_pulled_up_head_state` goes through `checkpoint_state`, so the epoch precompute's state is reused;
- `get_current_target_score` resolves one checkpoint per distinct `(root, epoch)` vote, not per vote.

A `lean_beacon_fast_confirmation_time_seconds` histogram times one run (buckets up to a mainnet slot). I did not measure it on a mainnet-size state; the numbers above are from reading the code, not from a profile.

**Safe-hash change.** `forkchoice_plan` calls `get_safe_execution_block_hash(store)`: the confirmed root's `checkpoint_hash` (bellatrix+: its payload hash; gloas: its bid's `parent_block_hash`; a block with no known payload, such as pre-bellatrix: zero, exactly as the finalized hash already behaves). Before the rule's first run, or while it is reset, the confirmed root is the finalized block, as the spec's initialization sets it.

**Departures from the Python** (all noted in the module doc): the live chain index with a block-table fallback for `store.blocks`; a missing `unrealized_justifications[root]` falls back to the store's justified checkpoint (as `get_voting_source` does) instead of raising; `is_one_confirmed` is false for an optimistic (`NOT_VALIDATED`) block, as the spec's prose requires; `get_slot_committee` returns a `Vec` (one slot's committees are disjoint); a validator index past a balance source's registry counts as inactive there; `CONFIRMATION_BYZANTINE_THRESHOLD` is a constant `25` (the key is not a `Config` field and stays in the ignored-keys warning).

## Ported tests

No FCR fixtures exist, so the pyspec scenarios are Rust unit tests in the module, on a fork-choice store built directly (fabricated blocks and post-states; votes cast into the latest messages one slot late as `on_attestation` applies them). The harness emulates the FFG justification a given participation produces (honest-chain rule), since it does not run the state transition. The tests are preset-agnostic and pass on both presets.

Ported (pyspec name, or the scenario):
- `test_basic`: `test_fast_confirm_an_epoch`, `..._with_low_participation`, `..._with_asynchrony_at_epoch_boundary`.
- `test_is_one_confirmed`: `..._passes_with_full_participation` (including the inequality terms), `..._fails_with_low_participation`, `..._support_accumulates_over_slots`, `..._slashing_non_supporters_helps`, `..._slashing_supporters_does_not_hurt`, `..._empty_slot_discount`, `..._epoch_crossing_block`, `..._fails_with_competing_branch`, `test_is_confirmed_chain_safe_passes_full_chain`; plus an optimistic-block case from the spec's prose.
- `test_empty_slots`: `test_fcr_handles_single_empty_slot`.
- `test_revert_finality`: `..._reverts_to_finalized_when_confirmed_not_canonical_mid_epoch`.
- `test_variables`: slot heads updated every slot, observed-justified rotation at the epoch start, initial values.
- Restart: the four cases of `get_restart_resilient_confirmed_root`, `block_should_be_finalized`, and the persisted-root hand-off (once per process).
- Gloas: the first step of `test_is_one_confirmed_delayed_with_mixed_payload_votes_in_empty_slot` (only FULL votes count as parent support in the empty slot, against every vote pre-gloas) and the `PENDING` node.

title: fix(metrics): serve the process collector's memory and CPU metrics
body:
The beacon dashboard's "Resident memory" panel reads `process_resident_memory_bytes{job="beacon"}`, which no ethlambda build exported. The `prometheus` crate only registers its process collector with the default registry when its `process` feature is on. Only the embedded-ethrex follower had it, because ethrex turns the feature on and features unify. Every other node's memory panel was blank, eth-2, eth-3 and eth-4 included.

### What changed

- `Cargo.toml`: `prometheus = { version = "0.14", features = ["process"] }`. On Linux the default registry, which `/metrics` gathers from (`gather_default_metrics`), now carries `process_resident_memory_bytes`, `process_virtual_memory_bytes`, `process_cpu_seconds_total`, `process_open_fds`, `process_max_fds`, `process_threads` and `process_start_time_seconds`, read from `/proc/self` at each scrape. Other platforms are unchanged.
- `Cargo.lock`: adds `procfs`/`procfs-core` 0.17.0, plus the older `rustix` 0.38 and `linux-raw-sys` 0.4 they depend on. `make cooldown-check` passes.
- `docs/metrics.md`: the process metrics, under Node Info Metrics.
- A Linux-only unit test that the default registry serves `process_resident_memory_bytes`, so dropping the feature fails CI instead of blanking the dashboard.

### Tests

- `make lint` clean, `make cooldown-check` passes (macOS; the new test is compiled out there).
