title: chore(deps): bump rustls, quick-xml, zstd-sys, ruint and quinn-proto past RustSec advisories, and drop libp2p's unused transports
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

`cargo audit` against `main` reports 14 advisories in the root lockfile and
11 in `tooling/event-monitor`'s. This PR is the follow-up #718 announced:
the `rustls` set has cleared the 14-day publish-age cooldown, and so have
fixes for `quick-xml`, `zstd-sys` and `ruint`. It also stops compiling
libp2p's DNS, mDNS, websocket, relay, kad and upnp transports, which the
swarm never builds from, so `hickory-dns` leaves the build graph instead
of waiting on a fork rebase.

## What Changed

Lockfiles, via `make update UPDATE_ARGS="-p ..."` so the cooldown is applied:

| Crate | From → to | Advisories fixed | Reachable here? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rustls` (both lockfiles) | 0.23.40 → 0.23.46 | 0285 (TLS 1.3 handshake messages accepted across encryption levels), 0346, 0348, 0349 | **Yes**: libp2p-quic/libp2p-tls on every QUIC peer, plus `reqwest` |
| `quick-xml` via `inferno` 0.12.6 → 0.12.8 | 0.39.4 → 0.41.0 | 0194, 0195 (CVSS 7.5) | No: only `inferno`'s flamegraph SVG under `jemalloc_pprof` |
| `zstd-sys` | 2.0.16 → 2.1.2 | 0410 | No: wasm allocator shim |
| `ruint` | 1.18.0 → 1.20.1 | 0220 | Reached through leanVM's `xmss` → `ethereum_ssz`; adds `ark-ff` 0.6 to the lock as an inactive optional dep |
| `quinn-proto` (event-monitor only) | 0.11.16 → 0.11.19 | 0185, 0338, 0339, 0340, 0342 | Same set #718 fixed on the root lockfile |

`rustls-webpki`, `rustls-pki-types`, `webpki-roots` and `aws-lc-rs`/`aws-lc-sys` move to the newest version the cooldown allows, which is what lets `rustls` reach 0.23.46.

`crates/net/p2p/Cargo.toml`: `libp2p` goes from `features = ["full"]` to the eleven features the swarm is built from (`ed25519`, `gossipsub`, `identify`, `macros`, `noise`, `quic`, `request-response`, `secp256k1`, `tcp`, `tokio`, `yamux`). That removes ~40 crates from the lock: the unsound `rand` 0.7 family, `webpki-roots` 0.26, `soketto`, `sysinfo`, `libp2p-{autonat,dcutr,floodsub,kad,ping,plaintext,pnet,relay,rendezvous,uds,websocket,...}`.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- No Rust source touched. Every lockfile bump is semver-compatible; `make cooldown-check` passes on both manifests.
- The libp2p feature list is derived from the `libp2p::` modules the p2p crate imports and the `SwarmBuilder` calls in `build_swarm` (`with_tcp`, `with_quic`, `with_behaviour`); `cargo check` and the p2p tests confirm nothing else was in use.
- `hickory-proto` and `libp2p-{dns,mdns,metrics,upnp}` still appear in `Cargo.lock`, so `cargo audit` keeps reporting RUSTSEC-2026-0118/0119. That is cargo's lock resolver keeping optional deps that a weak feature (`libp2p-dns?/tokio`) names; `cargo tree -i hickory-proto` shows no dependent, and nothing links it.

After this PR `cargo audit` reports 6 advisories on the root lockfile (down
from 14) and 2 on event-monitor's (down from 11): `rustls-webpki`,
`webpki-roots`/`webpki-root-certs` and `libz-sys` fixes still inside the
cooldown (until 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-11), `crypto-bigint` (needs `k256`
0.14 upstream), and the lock-only `hickory-proto` entry described above.

## Tests Added / Run

None added: no source touched.

- `make cooldown-check` (resolver probe on both manifests): passes
- `make lint`: clean
- `cargo test -p ethlambda-p2p`: 362 passed
- `make test`: 2868 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo audit`: 14 → 6 (root), 11 → 2 (event-monitor)

## Related Issues / PRs

- Follow-up to #718
- Next follow-up: `rustls-webpki` / `webpki-roots` / `webpki-root-certs` after 2026-11-03, `libz-sys` after 2026-11-11

title: perf(ssz-tree): hash merkle layers through sha2's block-level compression
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

Every inner node of the beacon state's merkle tree is SHA-256 of exactly 64 bytes: one data block plus one constant padding block. Going through `Digest` per pair buffers, pads and finalizes generically for each of the millions of pairs per state root. This hashes whole layers through `sha2::compress256` instead.

## What Changed

- `crates/common/ssz-tree/src/batch.rs` (new): hashes a whole layer with `sha2::compress256` directly (initial state, the pair, the fixed padding block, read the state out). sha2 still selects its hardware backend at run time, so the same SHA extensions are used.
- `crates/common/ssz-tree/src/tree.rs`: `fold_roots` folds each level in place through it; leaf roots (packed chunks and composite element roots) use a local `merkleize` built on the same primitive. The rayon fan-out above `PARALLEL_HASH_HEIGHT` is unchanged. Element roots of composite values still come from libssz.
- `crates/common/ssz-tree/Cargo.toml`: enables the `compress` feature of the `sha2` already in the lockfile (`compress256` is gated behind it). No new crate.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- Output is byte-identical to `hash_nodes(&Sha2Hasher, ..)`; no root changes, so no consensus or storage change.

## Tests Added / Run

- New tests in `batch.rs`: batched pairs and odd/even layers against `hash_nodes`, and a proptest of `merkleize` against libssz's. `batch_bench` (ignored, run with `cargo test -p ethlambda-ssz-tree --profile release-fast -- --ignored --nocapture batch_bench`) times old against new on a 2^20 layer fold, a fresh `List<u64>` root and a fresh `List<Validator>` root.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `make lint`: clean
- `cargo test --profile release-fast -p ethlambda-ssz-tree -p ethlambda-types -p ethlambda-state-transition --lib --bins`: ssz-tree 75 passed (1 ignored: `batch_bench`), state-transition 630 passed (15 ignored: BLS/KZG fixture vectors), types 232 passed
- Not run locally: `make test` (spec suites); CI covers them.

title: perf(p2p): verify one KZG batch per block for fetched data columns
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

A range or by-root answer, or a batch of parked columns replayed after their parent imports, carries many columns of the same block. Each column was checked on its own blocking task with its own `verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch` call, and the chain actor heard nothing until every sidecar of the whole call was done, so data availability waited on the slowest block of the batch. And every fulu sidecar of a block carries the same signed header, so its BLS signature was verified once per sidecar.

## What Changed

Two commits:

1. **One KZG batch per block** (`p2p/src/beacon/column_checks.rs`, `state_transition/src/beacon/gossip/column.rs`, and `fork_choice::verify_column_cells_batch`, one `verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch` call over every cell of several columns): `check_and_forward` groups the sidecars by block (the signed header's root for fulu, `beacon_block_root` for gloas). A group takes one `column_check_permits` permit, runs every sidecar's rules that do not read the cells, then verifies the proofs of all sidecars still standing in one batch. The group's `Keep` and `AwaitParent` sidecars go to the chain actor as soon as the group finishes. `chain_checks` is now `chain_precheck` followed by a KZG step, and gossip's `stateful_checks`/`stateful_checks_gloas` keep their order through the same split halves.
2. **Shared header signature verified once per group**: `SignatureMemo` remembers `header_signature_is_valid`'s answer for the group, keyed on the header root, the signature bytes and (for the head-state check made before parking) the head it read, so a forged signature over a shared header is judged on its own. The memo lives in one group's `spawn_blocking` closure; gossip and the single-sidecar wrappers use a fresh one per call.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- Verdicts do not change. The proofs are the last rule on the chain path (the lookahead rule after them is gossip's alone). A batch that fails is re-run sidecar by sidecar, so exactly the sidecars rejected before are rejected.
- Only the header signature's answer is memoized; every other rule runs per sidecar in its order.

## Tests Added / Run

- Measured locally: a batch over 9-blob columns costs 3.3x less than separate calls at 8 columns and 4.8x less at 32.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `make lint`: clean
- `cargo test --profile release-fast -p ethlambda-state-transition -p ethlambda-p2p --lib --bins`: state-transition 634 passed (16 ignored), p2p 364 passed (1 ignored)
- Not run locally: `make test` (spec suites); CI covers them.

Part of a beacon import perf batch, each PR independent and based on `main`: #752 (validation contention metrics, also edits `column_checks.rs` and `docs/metrics.md`), #753 (merkle layer hashing). The engine/STF overlap PR also edits `fork_choice.rs`, in a different region.

title: perf(blockchain): run the beacon state transition while the engine verdict is in flight
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

With an execution client, a pre-gloas beacon import waited for `engine_newPayload` and then ran the state transition, so the two summed. The request is now built on the actor and sent from a spawned task, and the actor computes the transition meanwhile, so the import costs the larger of the two.

This is possible because the transition reads the engine's verdict in one place (`process_execution_payload`), and `on_block` maps every verdict except `INVALIDATED` to `ExecutionEngine::valid()`. A transition computed assuming a valid payload is therefore the one `on_block` would run for every verdict it imports.

## What Changed

- `fork_choice.rs`: `speculate_transition` computes the block's transition against its parent's post-state with a `valid()` engine and returns it as a local value (`SpeculativeTransition`). `on_block_speculative` is `on_block` with an optional speculation: every check runs unchanged and in the same order; only the `transition_block` call is replaced, and only when the speculation was computed for this block root and parent root and the verdict is not `INVALIDATED`. `on_block` keeps its signature as a wrapper, so spec-test runners and the replay harness (no engine) are untouched.
- `beacon_engine.rs`: `OwnedNewPayloadRequest` (copies only the payload, never the block, so the request can move into a task) and `ask_request`.
- `lib.rs` (`process_block`): spawns the request, runs `speculate_transition`, awaits the task, then hands the speculation to `on_block_speculative`.
- `import_timing.rs`: the transition that overlapped the round trip is reported under `stf`, and `engine` reports only the wait left after it, so the rows still tile the end-to-end time. A discarded speculation leaves `engine` covering the overlap.
- `metrics.rs`: `lean_engine_speculation_total{outcome}` counts used and discarded attempts.
- `docs/beacon_engine.md`, `docs/benchmarking.md`, `docs/metrics.md`.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

| Verdict | Speculative post-state |
|---|---|
| `VALID`, or `SYNCING`/`ACCEPTED` for an optimistic candidate | used |
| `INVALIDATED` | dropped; `on_block` recomputes with `invalid()`, the invalidation path is unchanged |
| no answer, or `SYNCING`/`ACCEPTED` for a non-candidate | dropped; the block is held as before |
| computed for another root or parent | dropped |

- Nothing reaches the store, a non-content-addressed cache or the network until `on_block_speculative` accepts the speculation.
- A panicked or cancelled request task is treated as no verdict, like an exhausted retry ladder.
- Without an execution client, and for forks with no request to send (pre-merge, gloas), nothing overlaps and the path is the old one. The gloas envelope path (`beacon_envelope.rs`) is unchanged: it still runs the consensus checks before asking the execution client.
- The overlap is real on the production runtime: the chain actor runs on `Backend::Thread`, whose thread blocks on a multi-thread tokio `Runtime`, so the spawned request progresses on that runtime's workers while the actor computes.

## Tests Added / Run

- New `fork_choice` tests: a matching speculation leaves the store exactly as importing without one; it is the transition `on_block` uses; a speculation for another root or parent is ignored; an `INVALIDATED` verdict ignores it and matches today's result; no speculation without a parent state.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `make lint`: clean
- `cargo test --profile release-fast -p ethlambda-state-transition -p ethlambda-blockchain --lib --bins`: state-transition 635 passed (15 ignored), blockchain 293 passed (43 ignored)
- Not run locally: `make test` (spec suites); CI covers them.
- Not yet run against a live execution client in isolation. It runs on ethlambda-5's mainnet node (nightly with this batch, paired with ethrex v30.0.1), where `lean_engine_speculation_total{outcome}` shows how often the speculation is used.

title: feat(bench): split the beacon import's stf phase into steps, classes and resources
body:
## 🗒️ Description / Motivation

The import replay reported `stf` as one number. That is most of a mainnet block's import, but it does not say which step of the transition to attack, nor whether an epoch-crossing block, a block after skipped slots and an ordinary block differ. The beacon STF had no internal timing at all.

## What Changed

- `crates/blockchain/state_transition/src/metrics.rs`, `stf/*.rs`, `fork_choice.rs`: `lean_beacon_stf_phase_seconds{context,phase}` is observed around the steps of the transition: `process_slots` (excluding epoch work), `process_epoch`, the block signature, header (including the body hash it commits to), randao, eth1 data, execution payload (gloas: parent payload, withdrawals, bid), each operation list, the sync aggregate and the post-state root check. One `Instant` pair per step, none per attestation; an empty list observes nothing. The phase list is generated with the enum the code observes through, so the two cannot disagree.
- The `context` label: the epoch precompute worker runs `process_epoch` on another thread while an import runs, and the replay reads the histogram before and after each block, so one series would charge the worker to whichever block was importing. Only `fork_choice`'s `transition_block` sets `import` (a thread-local guard, since the steps are observed deep inside the per-fork block processing); every other caller writes `other`. The replay reads only `import`.
- `bin/ethlambda/src/benchmark/`: the replay report (`schema_version` 2) gains per block the STF steps, the stf time outside any step, a class (`epoch_boundary`, `after_skip`, `ordinary`), process CPU seconds and RSS; and per run p95 and p99, a per-class summary and the deltas of the cache lookup counters, so precompute hit rates appear in it.
- `docs/benchmarking.md`, `docs/metrics.md`.

## Correctness / Behavior Guarantees

- Consensus behavior is unchanged: the new code reads clocks around existing steps and never changes what is verified or in what order.

## Tests Added / Run

On this branch (based on `main`): `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `make lint` and `cargo test --profile release-fast -p ethlambda-state-transition -p ethlambda --lib --bins` are running; results will be posted as a comment.

On the adaptation of this change onto `nightly` (which carries the BLS stack):
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean; `make lint`: clean
- `cargo test --profile release-fast -p ethlambda-state-transition -p ethlambda-blockchain -p ethlambda-crypto --lib --bins`: 649 + 292 + 47 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --profile release-fast -p ethlambda --bins`: 287 passed, 4 ignored

Not run locally: `make test` (spec suites) and the minimal-preset beacon spec tests; CI covers them.

The BLS stack (#738) moves block signature checks into a deferred batch, so whichever of the two merges second adapts the phases to it. The `nightly` adaptation does it this way: a new phase `batch_signatures` (observed in `SignatureBatch::verify`, including the failure re-check loop); `randao`, the operation lists and `sync_aggregate` then cover set building and state changes only; `block_signature` is the proposer signature alone, which #738 still checks immediately.
